full_text: D 005 00 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Inclement Weather Policy Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order establishing an inclement weather policy for state employees. A. Background & Need The State of Colorado experiences severe weather conditions throughout the year. Colorado State government must continue to fully operate during these circumstances. However, extreme weather conditions may require the closure of certain State facilities. In these extraordinary circumstances the Governor or the Executive Directors of the Departments of State government must have the authority to make reasonable decisions regarding such closures. B. Directive All employees of the Executive Branch of State government are expected to work pursuant to assigned schedules regardless of weather conditions, subject to the provisions of this order. 1. Inclement weather will cause the closure of State facilities only in the event of extreme weather conditions. 2. The existence of extreme weather conditions shall be determined by the Governor or his Chief of Staff for all state facilities within the Denver Metropolitan area. The Denver Metropolitan area is defined as Denver and its surrounding suburbs within a 15-mile radius. 3. Executive Directors, or their designated representatives, are delegated the authority to close State facilities outside of the Denver Metropolitan area during times of severe weather. In addition, Executive Directors are delegated the authority to stagger the release times of employees when severe weather conditions exist that warrant such action. 4. If the Governor or Executive Directors close state facilities, affected employees will be granted administrative leave subject to the following provisions: i. State facilities and employees necessary to the health and safety of the state must remain in service during extreme weather conditions. Executive Directors shall pre- determine which functions within their respective departments are necessary during extreme weather conditions. State employees who are required to work during a closure will remain on their regular pay rate and will not be granted a future day of administrative leave. 2 ii. State employees who arrive late to work due to severe weather conditions, when the State facility has not been closed, may be excused only if the appointing authority determines, in his or her discretion, that the lateness was reasonable. iii. State employees who are already on approved leave when a closure occurs may not substitute administrative leave for the period of closure. iv. Emergency road closures made by State, county or municipal governments or by the Colorado State Patrol will be honored by the State. State employees affected by state or local road closures may be granted administrative leave. v. Higher education institutions are exempt from this order and may establish an independent policy based upon the institutions’ respective needs. vi. If the Governor determines that weather conditions amount to a “disaster” within the meaning of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, the provisions of the Act as described at C.R.S. 24-32-2114 will be implemented. C. Responsibilities The following responsibilities are assigned to implement this order: 1. The Governor’s Press Secretary or the Chief of Staff will be the point of contact in the Governor’s Office for inclement weather matters. 2. The Colorado State Patrol shall keep the Governor’s Office informed on road conditions and closures. 3. The Executive Directors of the Departments of State government shall designate in advance those employees who are necessary during extreme weather conditions. In addition, Executive Directors shall develop an internal procedure to process inclement weather decisions, including a system of notification for employees. D. Past Executive Orders Superceded and Replaced Past Executive Orders and policies concerning the inclement weather policy for State employees are hereby superceded and replaced by this Executive Order, including the Inclement Weather Policy of November 1, 1988. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado The 22nd day of May, 2000. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 006 01 EXECUTIVE ORDER PROCLAMATION CALL FOR FIRST EXTRAORDINARY SESSION OF THE SIXTY-THIRD GENERAL ASSEMBLY Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and in particular vested in the Governor pursuant to Article IV, Section 9 of the Colorado Constitution, and as provided for in Article V, Section 7, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order convening the Sixty-Third General Assembly to meet in special session. 1. Background and Need Colorado’s economic activity and population continue to grow rapidly. According to the 2000 United States Census report, Colorado’s population has increased by thirty percent to a record 4.3 million people over the past ten years. This increase in population has occurred primarily on the Front Range of Colorado and the impacts are readily apparent to native and newcomer alike. Colorado citizens have consistently stated that the rapid population growth threatens our state’s unique quality of life. Colorado’s voters and its legislature have struggled with the question of how to manage the benefits associated with the population increase and how to reduce the harmful impacts of the development that have resulted. If the State of Colorado fails to wisely manage its unprecedented growth, we risk losing a lifestyle found in no other place in the country. Unfortunately, despite attempts in three successive legislative sessions and a citizen’s initiative to address this difficult issue, Colorado still does not have a solution. Because there has been no resolution concerning how to address this most pressing issue for Colorado, in my opinion an extraordinary occasion has arisen that necessitates that I convene a special session of the legislature to answer the needs of the people of Colorado. 2. Proclamation I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, convene the Sixty-Third General Assembly of this state and summon the members of the Sixty-Third General Assembly to meet in Special Session at the State Capitol, in the City and County of Denver, on May 10, 2001, at 12:00 p.m. and designate the following subjects for your consideration and appropriate legislative action: A. Concerning the creation of mandatory and binding comprehensive planning documents containing planning elements to protect open space, ensure coordination of infrastructure and capital facilities, promote the goal of orderly development and protect traditional rural lifestyles that ensure the fair and equitable treatment of all private property owners affected by the plans in jurisdictions with significant urban populations or that are experiencing a rapid rate of population growth as measured by the Colorado Department of Local Affairs. B. Concerning an appropriation for the Office of Smart Growth located in the Colorado Department of Local Affairs. C. Concerning the creation of an alternative dispute resolution system between and among cities and counties regarding conflicts between the mandatory comprehensive plans or disputes arising out of the mandatory comprehensive planning process. D. Concerning allowing property owners adjacent to a proposed annexation in which the contiguity requirements in C.R.S. 31-12-104 (1)(a) are achieved by annexing a platted street or alley, a public or private right of way, a public or private transportation right of way or area, or a lake, reservoir, stream or other natural or artificial waterway, the opportunity to be included in the proposed annexation. E. Concerning the authorization of a regional planning agreement within the jurisdiction of the metropolitan planning organization (MPO) for the Denver metropolitan area that upholds local decision-making authority. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this _____ day of May, 2001. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 008 01 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Strengthening Colorado’s Administrative Justice System Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order regarding the State Administrative Justice System. 1. Purpose. A substantial number of Coloradans depend on administrative adjudication to resolve their disputes in matters including, but not limited to, occupational licensing, workers' compensation, the operation of the state personnel system, and human services benefits. Consistent management and accountability is required to ensure that Colorado's administrative justice system provides efficient and fair resolution of these matters. This order is designed to provide for the effective management of the State's administrative justice system, through preserving the decisional independence of administrative adjudicatory personnel while also effectively implementing the purposes of state agencies, regardless of whether administrative adjudicative personnel or functions are lodged in the Division of Administrative Hearings. 2. Standards of Professional Conduct. To ensure the decisional independence of administrative adjudicative personnel and to protect the rights of Colorado citizens, all administrative law judges shall adhere to the Colorado Code of Judicial Conduct. The Executive Director of the Department of Personnel shall establish and implement appropriate standards of conduct for hearing officers and any other executive branch official who exercises independent legal judgment in the conduct of quasi-judicial hearings to adjudicate justiciable interests between adverse parties. Officials of affected agencies shall cooperate with the Executive Director of the Department of Personnel to ensure that the standards of conduct are enforced with respect to both the administrative adjudicative personnel and personnel responsible for the development and implementation of substantive agency policies. The Executive Director of the Department of Personnel may require training for administrative adjudicatory personnel, so long as such training is provided at no cost to affected agencies. The Executive Director of the Department of Personnel shall report to the Governor regarding the condition of the State's administrative justice system, along with recommendations for improvement or reform, on or before July 1, 2002. 2 3. Intra-Governmental Coordination. By the authority vested in me by Article IV of the Colorado Constitution and that vested in the respective Executive Directors by § 24-1-107, C.R.S. and other applicable statutes, I hereby authorize and direct the following officials to coordinate their administrative law judges and associated support staff with the Executive Director of the Department of Personnel: • The Executive Director of the Department of Labor and Employment and the Director of the Division of Workers' Compensation; • The State Personnel Board; • The Executive Director of the Department of Regulatory Agencies and the Public Utilities Commission; and • The Executive Director of the Department of Corrections and the State Parole Board. Such coordination may occur, within the scope of existing constitutional and statutory authority, through a written delegation, memorandum of understanding, or both, and may place budgetary, personnel, legal, and programmatic authority, as well as pertinent property, documents, and records, under the direction of the Executive Director of the Department of Personnel. All affected personnel shall retain all rights under the state personnel system and retirement benefits under the laws of this state, and their services shall be deemed to have been continuous. The Executive Director of the Department of Personnel may also provide administrative law judges on a contractual basis to governmental entities other than those required to use services from the Division, or to obviate potential conflicts, on such terms and conditions as he or she may deem appropriate. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado ________ Day of May, 2001. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 003 02 Executive Order Transferring Funds to the Office of Energy Management and Conservation to Conduct the Low -Cost Weatherization Program Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order transferring funds to the Office of Energy Management and Conservation to conduct the low-cost weatherization program. 1. Background and Need. The U.S. Department of Health and Human Services is the recipient of funds under the Low- Income Home Energy Assistance Act of 1981 (P.L. 97-35) hereafter referred to as the Low- Income Energy Assistance Program (LIEAP). The Colorado Department of Human Services is the recipient of funds for the LIEAP Program. The Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Act of 1981 allows up to 15 percent of the funds to be used for low-cost residential weatherization or other energy related home repair for low-income households. Low cost residential weatherization services for Colorado’s low-income population will provide long-range benefits for Colorado. The Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation is best able to use the weatherization funds to serve Colorado’s low- income population. 2. Mission and Order. I hereby designate the Office of Energy Management and Conservation as the responsible agency to administer a low-cost weatherization program. The low-cost weatherization program shall be administered in accordance with state and federal laws and regulations. The Colorado Department of Human Services shall transfer $4,065,984 to the Office of Energy Management and Conservation to conduct a low-cost weatherization program. Of the total, $ 4,025,937 shall be drawn from the LIHEAP Block Grant and $40,047 from the Leveraging Incentive Program award. 3. Past Executive Orders Modified and Replaced. This Executive Order shall supercede and replace all previous executive orders regarding the designation of the agency responsible for administering the Low-Income Energy Assistance Program. 4. Duration. This Executive Order shall remain in effect until further modification or rescission by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this _____ day of February, 2002. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 008 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat of Wildfires Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2104, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order making certain funds available from the Emergency Management Fund for wildfire mitigation and preparation activities. 1. Background and Purpose. The State of Colorado must prepare for another challenging wildfire season. Last year, 4,612 fires burned 619,030 acres. These fires destroyed 384 homes and 624 non- residential structures. The exact cost of this destruction is still being calculated, however, a conservative estimate places it well above $100 million. Most tragically, the fires of 2002 claimed the lives of nine wildland firefighters. On April 23, 2002, I signed Executive Order D 009 02, which made state disaster funds available to pre-position Single Engine Air Tankers with the objective of putting out fires while they are still controllable. This proved to be a successful plan. The Colorado Forest Service reported that 92% of the 2002 fires were kept below 10 acres. Due to last year’s high-risk wildfire conditions, fires that escaped initial attack quickly became the largest and most destructive wildfires in state history. The State of Colorado must begin preparing for another dangerous wildfire season. Even with the most recent snowstorm, the current Drought Monitor shows approximately 75% of Colorado is still in extreme drought conditions. Summer temperatures are predicted to be above normal and moisture levels of fuel sources (brush and wood) are at risk of falling well below average during the fire season. Coincidentally, many federal aviation resources have been necessarily diverted to non-fire threats and the remaining federal aviation resources will have to be shared amongst wildfires throughout the country. State and local resources, both ground and air, will be more heavily relied upon during this fire season. For these reasons, I believe that the State of Colorado must take proactive measures to prepare for the 2003 wildfire season. As envisioned by the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, threats to the public safety of this magnitude confer upon the Governor unique powers and responsibilities. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-32-2104 (1). The Act defines disasters as the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire. C.R.S. § 24-32- 2103 (1.5). The purpose of the Disaster Emergency Act is to reduce the vulnerability of injury to the people of Colorado and damage to property located within the state. C.R.S. § 24-32-2102(1). Extensive resources are immediately necessary to increase the level of fire suppression capability to reduce the imminent threat of wildfires. In accordance with the Disaster Emergency Act, I issue this Executive Order making certain Emergency Management Funds immediately available for wildfire mitigation and preparation activities. These activities include the pre-positioning of Single Engine Air Tankers and staffing additional wildland interface fire engines. 2. Mission. I hereby declare that the imminent threat of wildfires constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order $1,672,811 in disaster emergency funds be made immediately available for wildfire mitigation and preparation activities. These funds shall remain available for this purpose until September 1, 2003. 3. Duration. This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. It is within my authority to extend this Executive Order every thirty days until the imminent threat of wildfires has passed. GIVEN under my hand and t h e E x e c u t i v e S e a l o f t h e State of Colorado, this ___ day of April, 2003. B i l l O w e n s G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 013 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Directing State Departments Responsible for Public Safety to Adopt a Single Regional Planning Map for Emergency Management and Response Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing state departments to recognize and adopt a single regional planning and operations map for purposes of emergency management and response. 1. Background and Purpose. State and local governments must continue to improve their ability to respond to public safety threats. To that end, it is imperative that different levels of government are able to cooperate with one another in emergency management and response efforts. In Colorado, various state agencies are responsible for different aspects of public health and safety. These agencies have created and adopted numerous maps dividing the state into different regions for public health and safety purposes. Undoubtedly, local governments have experienced a similar development. This results in incompatible maps that could cause confusion among state and local agencies and require public health and safety managers to participate in redundant planning efforts. In order to ensure efficient emergency management, this Executive Order creates a single regional planning and operations map. This will enable state and local agencies to work together to provide integrated and cooperative emergency services to the citizens of Colorado. The Colorado General Assembly recommended that such a map be adopted through House Resolution 03-1018 and the following organizations have already agreed to adopt the single regional planning and operations map: Colorado Counties Incorporated, the Colorado Municipal League, the Colorado State Fire Chief’s Association, the Colorado Association of Chiefs of Police, the County Sheriff’s of Colorado, the Emergency Medical Services Association of Colorado, and the Colorado Emergency Management Association. Through this Executive Order, I set forth the single regional planning and operations map and direct all state departments to recognize and adopt this map. To ensure a congruent system, I urge local agencies to adopt this map for emergency management and response purposes. 2. Mission. I hereby order all state departments that are responsible for public health and safety to recognize and adopt the single regional planning and operations map for purposes of emergency management and response. The map shall be divided into the following nine regions: 1) Northwest : Eagle, Garfield, Grand, Jackson, Mesa, Moffat, Pitkin, Rio Blanco, Routt, and Summit Counties. 2) Northeast : Cheyenne, Larimer, Lincoln, Logan, Kit Carson, Morgan, Phillips, Sedgwick, Washington, Weld and Yuma Counties. 3) Northcentral : Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Clear Creek, Denver, Douglas, Elbert, Gilpin and Jefferson Counties. 4) Southcentral : Chaffee, El Paso, Lake, Park and Teller Counties. 5) West : Delta, Gunnison, Hinsdale, Montrose, Ouray and San Miguel Counties. 6) Southwest : Archuleta, Dolores, La Plata, Montezuma and San Juan Counties. 7) San Luis : Alamosa, Conejos, Costilla, Mineral, Rio Grande and Saguache Counties. 8) South : Custer, Fremont, Huerfano, Las Animas and Pueblo Counties. 9) Southeast : Baca, Bent, Crowley, Kiowa, Otero and Prowers Counties. 3. Duration. This Executive Order shall remain in force until modified or terminated by further executive order of the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and t h e E x e c u t i v e S e a l o f t h e State of Colorado, this ____ day of July, 2003. Bill Owens G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 017 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Establishing the Colorado Interagency Council on Homelessness Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order establishing the Colorado Interagency Council on Homelessness. 1. Background and Need Homelessness in Colorado has changed over the past decade. The homeless population has become increasingly dominated by families with children. There were an estimated 9,725 persons in the seven-county Denver metropolitan area who were homeless as of January 2003. One third of these people, 3,059, were children and families. It is estimated that the annual rate of homelessness in just the Denver-metro area is more than 31,000 persons each year. Roughly 71 percent of the homeless population were sleeping in emergency shelters, on the streets or in their car, were camping out, staying night-to-night at welfare hotels, or just coming out of institutions with nowhere to go. Chronic homelessness affects both single individuals and families. Half of the homeless population in the seven-county metropolitan area had been homeless for less than 90 days, and more than 10 percent had been homeless for more than two years. Reasons for homelessness include unemployment, inability to pay rent or mortgage, substance abuse, mental illness, and domestic violence. 2. Mission and Scope A. The Homeless Policy Academy was an interagency working group organized within the Colorado Department of Human Services. The Colorado Department of Human Services will terminate the Homeless Policy Academy and transfer all duties, authorities, and funding to the Colorado Interagency Council on Homelessness created by this Executive Order. B. The Homeless Policy Academy functioned as the State of Colorado’s authority on homeless issues. The Colorado Interagency Council on Homelessness will assume the duties, authority, and funding previously belonging to the Academy. C. The Council shall operate with existing state resources and staff with which the Homeless Policy Academy currently operates. Funds from grants and foundations will continue to be permitted. D. The Governor shall appoint Council members or may delegate appointment authority to department directors, and shall choose two liaisons between the state Council and the federal Interagency Council who will act as co chairs of the Council. Council members shall serve at the pleasure of the Governor, or if appointed by department director, members shall serve at the discretion of the department director. E. The Council shall serve as the advisory body to the Governor on housing needs and homeless issues. The Council shall make recommendations to the cochairs on homeless policy and funding priorities. F. Council activities may include developing an outreach and education campaign to reduce the stigma of homelessness, increasing access to mainstream resources such as TANF or CHP + assistance, expanding and maximizing service resources such as mental health/substance abuse services, expanding and maximizing housing resources, and improving cross system policies and procedures such as intake processes at shelters. 2. Directive The Colorado Interagency Council on Homelessness is hereby created. The Council will assume all duties, authority, and funding previously maintained by the Homeless Policy Academy. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. Given under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this _________ day of October, 2003. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 003 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat of Wildfires Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2104, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order making certain funds available from the Emergency Management Fund for wildfire mitigation and preparation activities. 1. Background and Purpose. The State of Colorado must begin to prepare for the 2004 wildfire season. Colorado continues to face drought conditions throughout most of the state. The United States Department of Agriculture monitors drought conditions and recently reported that all of Colorado was in the “Abnormally Dry” to “Extreme Drought” categories. While we continue to hope for significant precipitation this spring, we must take measures to ensure that the State of Colorado is prepared for an active wildfire season. The wildfires of 2001 demonstrated that it is nearly impossible to stop a full-blown wildfire in drought conditions. For this reason, I began focusing state resources towards mitigating wildfire risks and extinguishing wildfires before they become uncontrollable. For the past two years, I have made state disaster emergency funds available several months before the wildfire season in order to staff wildfire mitigation activities and contract wildfire early response equipment. This has been an extremely effective strategy. The Colorado Forest Service reported that 95.5% of the 2003 fires were controlled at under 10 acres. The 4.5% of fires that became uncontrollable burned 22,160 acres or 95% of the total acreage burnt in 2003. Similar results were achieved the previous year. Mitigation and suppression activities have proven to be a successful tool for minimizing damage caused by wildfires. Wildfires pose a dangerous threat to Colorado citizens’ lives and property. I am committed to taking decisive and forceful measures to mitigate the destructive consequences of wildfires. As envisioned by the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, threats to the public safety of this magnitude confer upon the Governor unique powers and responsibilities. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters (C.R.S. § 24-32-2104 (1)). The Act defines disasters as the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire (C.R.S. § 24-32-2103 (1.5)). The purpose of the Disaster Emergency Act is to reduce the vulnerability of injury to the people of Colorado and damage to property located within the state (C.R.S. § 24-32-2102(1)(a)) and provide for coordination of activities relating to disaster prevention, preparedness and response by the state (C.R.S. § 24-32 –2102(1)(f)). In order to reduce the imminent threat of wildfires, extensive resources are immediately necessary to increase the level of fire mitigation and suppression capability. In accordance with the Disaster Emergency Act, I issue this Executive Order making certain Emergency Management Funds immediately available for wildfire mitigation and preparedness activities. These activities include the pre-positioning of Single Engine Air Tankers and staffing additional wildland interface fire engines. 2. Directive. I hereby declare that the imminent threat of wildfires constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order $1.1 million in disaster emergency funds be made immediately available for wildfire mitigation and preparation activities. These funds shall remain available for this purpose until December 31, 2004. 3. Duration. This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this ___ day of March, 2004. B i l l O w e n s G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 010 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER Implementation of the Colorado Benefits Management System Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning the implementation of the Colorado Benefits Management System. 1. Background and Need The Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS) is a state of the art eligibility and payment system for issuing benefits to clients across Colorado for a variety of social service programs administered by counties and select medical assistance sites. The Colorado Department of Human Services (DHS) and the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF) began developing CBMS in 1995 after receiving approval from the Colorado General Assembly and federal agencies. Increasingly complex programs and regulations drove the need for CBMS amid concerns that Colorado could no longer rely upon outdated technology and inconsistent methods of determining eligibility to state and federal programs. CBMS will replace six existing computer systems with one unified system for collecting data, establishing eligibility, and processing payments. CBMS will support the following federal and state programs: Temporary Assistance for Needy Families, Food Stamps, Medicaid, Adult Protective Services, Old Age Pension, Aid to the Blind, Aid to the Needy Disabled, and the Children’s Health Plan Plus. Federal and state laws and regulations related to these programs and eligibility requirements are not altered by the implementation of CBMS. CBMS will improve access to public assistance and medical benefits by integrating the functions of the existing automated systems, providing one-stop shopping for clients, permitting faster eligibility determinations, and providing increased accuracy and consistency in eligibility determinations and benefit calculations statewide. The Executive Directors of the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing and the Department of Human Services have decided that the transition to CBMS will begin on September 1, 2004. In implementing any comprehensive system as sophisticated as CBMS, we anticipate challenges during the transition period. This Executive Order is issued out of concern for Colorado citizens who are in need of assistance from DHS and HCPF, in a coordinated effort to ensure that eligible clients are not adversely affected by the process of transitioning between automated systems. 2. Directive A. I hereby direct the Executive Dir ectors of DHS and HCPF to employ backup systems and contingency plans to ensure that eligible applicants will not be denied benefits during the transition to CBMS. B. I hereby direct the Executive Dir ectors of DHS and HCPF to employ backup systems and contingency plans to protect the benefits of clients who maintain eligibility during the transition to CBMS. C. I hereby direct that an additional $2 million in federal funds from the Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003 be made available to counties through the Executive Directors of DHS and HCPF to assist the counties during this transitional period. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this _____ day of August, 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 003 05 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat of Wildfires Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2101 et seq., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order making certain funds available from the Emergency Management Fund for wildfire preparation and suppression activities. 1. Background and Purpose The State of Colorado must begin to prepare for the 2005 wildfire season. Despite mixed snow pack conditions this winter, Colorado continues to experience varying degrees of drought conditions throughout the state. The United States Department of Agriculture (the “USDA”) has again this year declared disaster status due to drought conditions in many rural Colorado counties. While we continue to hope for significant precipitation throughout the spring, we must take measures to ensure that the State of Colorado is prepared for another active wildfire season. Colorado is home to some 22.6 mi llion acres of fore sted lands—nearly two-thirds of which are federally owned. The USDA Forest Service, in coordination with other state and federal agencies, has determined that some 9 million forested acres in Colorado are so far overgrown and otherwise outside of their normal ecological condition that if a fire were to occur, the majority of the forests’ ecosystem components would be lost, including wildlife habitat components. Colorado’s recent experiences with wildfires demonstrate that it is nearly impossible to contain a high-intensity wildfire in drought conditions. For this reason, in the past three years I have focused state resources on mitigating wildfire risks and building the capability to contain wildfires before they become uncontrollable. Accordingly, I have proactively utilized state disaster emergency funds to pre-position wildfire-fighting resources for fire season. Recent history has proved this to be an extremely effective strategy. The Colorado State Forest Service reported that 94% of the 2004 non-federal land wildfires were controlled while occupying less than 10 acres. The 1% of fires that became uncontrollable burned 14,454 acres or 95% of the total acreage burnt in 2004. Similar suppression results were achieved the previous year. Consequently, mitigation a nd suppression activities have proven to be a successful tool for minimizing damage caused by wildfires. Wildfires pose a substantial threat to Colo rado citizens’ lives and property, and have detrimental effects on wildlife habitat, air quality, and water quality. I am committed to taking decisive and forceful measures to mitigate these destructive consequences of wildfires. As envisioned by the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act (the “Act”), threats to the public safety of this magnitude c onfer upon the Gover nor unique powers and responsibilities. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting dangers to our state presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-32-2104(1). The Act defines disasters as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespre ad or severe damage, injury , or loss of lif e or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire . . . .” C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). The purpose of the Act is to reduce the vulnerability of injury to the people of Colorado and damage to property located within the state and provide for coordination of ac tivities relating to disaster prevention, preparedness and response by the state. C.R.S. § 24-32-2102(1)(a) and (f). In order to reduce the imminent threat of wildfires, extensive resources are necessary to increase the level of fire mitigation and suppression capability. In accordance with the Act, this Executive Order makes certain f unds available for wildfire mitigation and preparedness activities. In order to permit contractual commitment of the funds for the 2005 wildfire season, all of the funds allocated by this Order and required for 2005 wildfire preparedness activities will be available immediately. 2. Directive a. I hereby declare that the imminent threat of wildfires constitutes a disaster, as defined by C.R.S. § 24-32-2103. b. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order $2,950,000 in disaster emergency funds be available until November 1, 2005. c. I order an additional $350,000, which will be paid from federal funds received pursuant to Public Law 108-27, be made immediately available for funding the essential government services desc ribed herein and remain available through December 31, 2005. d. The disaster emergency funds and fe deral funds allocate d by this order, totaling $3,300,000, shall be used to implement the 2005 Initial Air Attack Plan that includes the contracting of Single Engine Air Tankers and call when needed helicopters specifically equipped to fight wildfires and also to provide for other preparedness and mitigation resources. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this ________ day of March, 2005. B i l l O w e n s G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 004 07 EXECUTIVE ORDER Establishing a Preferred Drug List Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Ritter, Jr., Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order regarding the establishment of a preferred drug list for non-Medicare clients re ceiving drugs through the fee-for-service and primary care physician progr ams in the Colorado Medical Assistance Program. 1. Background and Purpose. The Medical Assistance Program operated by the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy & Financing (the “Department”) provides drug coverage to clients who are not also on Medicare. The Department has implemented a number of util ization mechanisms to control costs, but the amount spent on medications per client continues to grow. Due to the state of Colorado’s budget restrictions, it is imperative that the State of Co lorado does all that it ca n to control costs while continuing to protect vulnerable populations. Many other state Medicaid programs have esta blished a preferred drug list (“PDL”) and a number of those states have entered into multi -state purchasing pools. By establishing PDLs, these states have reported that they have been able to decrease expenditures while still providing needed medications to their participants. In es tablishing a PDL, states are also able to obtain supplemental rebates from drug companies. Obtaining supplemental rebates will allow Colorado the ability to provide medications at the lowest possible costs. In order to establish a PDL, states create a Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee. Although the exact duties of this Committee vary state to st ate, the Committee is usually responsible for comparing drugs on a clinical basis and recomme nding which drugs should be preferred agents on the PDL. The Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee typically consists of medical professionals who review evidence-based clinical data to make their recommendation. Pursuant to C.R.S. §25.5-5-506(3)(a), the Depart ment has the authority to implement drug utilization mechanisms to control costs in th e Medical Assistance Program associated with prescribed drugs. A PDL is an additional drug util ization mechanism that is necessary to further control the expenditures on drugs through the Medical Assistance Program. 2. Directives. A. Pursuant to C.R.S. §25.5-5-506, the Departme nt is hereby directed to establish and maintain a PDL for all fee-for-service and primary care physician Medical Assistance Program non-Medicare clients. B. The Department shall evaluate the various methods by which a PDL is implemented and maintained and shall determine the best option for Colorado’s PDL. The Department has the authority to take any actions it deems appropriate to create and maintain a PDL. C. The Department shall form a Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee, which will use clinical data and evidence in considering drugs for inclusion in the PDL. D. Any such PDL established by the Department shall comply with all state and federal laws. E. The Department shall also obtain supplemental rebates to further ensure that the State can provide drug coverage for Medical Assistance Program clients at the lowest possible cost. F. The Department is hereby directed to de termine the best method by which to obtain supplemental rebates. This shall include an evaluation of the feasibility and cost- effectiveness of entering into one of the existing multi-state purchasing pools. The evaluation shall focus on the costs and bene fits of each of these existing pools in comparison to alternative methods by whic h the Department may obtain supplemental rebates. G. After the evaluation is completed, the Department shall take any actions it deems appropriate to implement the method chosen to obtain supplemental rebates. The Department also has the authority to re-evalu ate the options available to the Department when it determines such re-evaluation is justified. H. There may be administrative costs associated with this implementation. The Department is permitted to request funding for such costs through the State budget process. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modificatio n or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this ____ day of January, 2007. Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor

full_text: D 012 09 EXECUTIVE ORDER Designating the Colorado Nonprofit Association as the State’s Authorized Entity for the ARRA-Strengthening Communities Fund-State, Local, Tribal Government Capacity Building Program Federal Grant Pursuant to the authority vested in the office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Ritter, Jr., Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order designating the Colorado Nonprofit Association as the State’s Authorized Entity to serve as the coordinating agency for the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009-Strengthening Communities Fund-State, Local, Tribal Government Capacity Building Program Grant (HHS-2009-ACF-OCS- 0092) (the “SCF Grant”). I. Background and Purpose A. Description of the SCF Grant The SCF Grant arises under the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act (“ARRA”) and is administered by the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (“HHS”). As described by HHS, the purpose of the SCF Grant is to build the capacity of government offices (and their designees) to assist nonprofit organizations in addressing the broad economic recovery issues present in their communities, including helping low- income individuals secure and retain employment, earn higher wages, obtain better- quality jobs, and gain greater access to state and federal benefits and tax credits. The SCF grant provides that a State may designate an Authorized Entity, through an executive order, to apply for and administer this grant. The Authorized Entity will serve as a coordinating agency for nonprofit organizations to access information and services with regard to ARRA efforts and benefits. Executive Order D 012 09 June 25, 2009 Page 2 of 4 B. Colorado’s need for the SCF Grant The economic downturn has negatively affected Colorado’s businesses and residents. In May 2009, the State’s overall unemployment rate was 7.6%. However, different regions of the State are experiencing greater economic challenges as indicated by the following county unemployment rates: in the northern part of the State, Weld County- 8.2%; in the Denver Metro area, Adams County -8.5% and the City and County of Denver – 8.0%; in the south, Pueblo County - 8.1%; in the San Luis Valley, Costilla County-10.2%; on the Western Slope, Mesa County-8.1%, Montrose County- 8.5% and Dolores County-14.9%. The SCF Grant will assist Colorado’s nonprofits and state and local governments in addressing the needs of these communities and doing so in the most efficient manner. While nonprofits and state and local government have existing working relationships in all regions of Colorado, these relationships can be made more effective, particularly around ARRA opportunities and economic recovery. Both governments and nonprofits could benefit from capacity building efforts that would increase communication, build stronger partnerships and establish more efficient ways of doing business between the government and nonprofit sectors. C. The Colorado Nonprofit Association and its SCF Grant partners Founded in 1986, the Colorado Nonprofit Association is a statewide membership organization that provides capacity-building and technical assistance resources to nonprofits in the form of educational workshops, training guides, consultation, conferences and communications on critical issues facing the sector. The Association also leads the nonprofit sector in influencing public policy and public opinion. The Association is well positioned to serve as the Authorized Entity under the SCF Grant. As a statewide organization, the Association works with nonprofits in many communities. Its Practices and Principles for Nonprofit Excellence serves as the essential training and best practices guide for nonprofits throughout Colorado. Since the enactment of ARRA, the Association has collected and distributed ARRA funding information to nonprofits through conferences, its website and newsletter. As a public policy advocacy organization, the Association engages with state and local government entities on behalf of the nonprofit sector. To effectively implement the SCF Grant, the Association has identified key strategic partners from across Colorado. The Association has partnered with the Denver Office of Strategic Partnerships to provide linkage between the City and County of Denver and nonprofit organizations within the City and the surrounding Metro Area. The Executive Order D 012 09 June 25, 2009 Page 3 of 4 Association will also include the Colorado Department of Local Affairs, the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment, the Colorado Department of Human Services, the Governor’s Commission on Community Service, the Colorado Municipal League, and Colorado Counties Inc. in carrying out SCF Grant activities. II. Directives A. The Colorado Nonprofit Association is hereby designated as the State’s Authorized Entity to apply for and administer the SCF Grant. B. I established the Colorado Economic Recovery Accountability Board to ensure that state and local agencies use ARRA funds with transparency, accountability and for the highest possible benefit. I direct the Board and its staff to make available pertinent information about ARRA funding programs and state agency ARRA plans to the Association for its activities under the SCF Grant. C. To facilitate the flow of information and to track progress, I direct the Association to report monthly on its SCF Grant activities to the Board Chair or his designee and to file a quarterly written report to the full Board. D. Agencies under my direct executive authority shall cooperate in the implementation of this Order. Specifically, I direct the Departments of Labor and Employment, Local Affairs, Human Services and the Governor’s Energy Office to provide the Association with access to agency information and program staff involved with ARRA funded programs, to consider the Association’s proposals to more effectively and efficiently involve nonprofits in participating in ARRA opportunities and to support the Association’s efforts under the SCF Grant to strengthen linkages between nonprofit organizations and state and local government agencies. I also direct the Association to report progress and activities to the Executive Directors of these departments on a monthly basis. E. Other entities of State government not under my direct executive authority are requested to assist in the Association’s efforts to provide capacity building and linkages between governments and nonprofits under the SCF Grant. Executive Order D 012 09 June 25, 2009 Page 4 of 4 III. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until modified or rescinded by future Executive Order of the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado T h i s 2 5 th day of June, 2009 Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor.

full_text: D 016 09 EXECUTIVE ORDER Approving and Authorizing the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority as the “Certifying Officer” Under the National Environmental Policy Act to the Extent Necessary to Implement the Tax Credit Assistance Program Contained in the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Ritter, Jr., Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order approving and authorizing the Colorado Housing and Finance Authority as the “Certifying Officer” under the National Environmental Policy Act to the extent necessary to implement the Tax Credit Assistance Program contained in the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. I. Background and Purpose On February 17, 2009, President Obama signed into law the American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009, which established the Tax Credit Assistance Program (“TCAP”) through an appropriation of $2.25 billion in special HOME funds. The purpose of the TCAP program is to facilitate the production of multifamily affordable rental developments that serve low income residents. The program provides a source of funds that will be used to fill financing gaps caused by the sharp decline in equity pricing within the multifamily rental market. The United States Department of Housing and Urban Development (“HUD”) has federal oversight of the program; yet housing credit agencies in each state are responsible for administering the program. In Colorado, pursuant to Colorado Executive Order D 0050 87, Colorado Housing and Finance Authority (“CHFA”) is designated as the state housing credit agency responsible for allocating the low-income housing tax credit program and, as such, has oversight responsibility for administering the TCAP program. Because the TCAP program is funded under an appropriation of special HOME funds, a substantial portion of the federal HOME provisions apply to the administration of the program. As an example, the State government must assume the federal environmental review responsibility contained in the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (“NEPA”). States, however, may authorize state housing credit agencies to carry out these federal environmental Executive Order D 016 09 August 6, 2009 Page 2 of 2 review responsibilities on behalf of the State. I am designating the Executive Director of the Colorado Housing Finance Authority or his designee as the “Certifying Officer” as defined in 24 C.F.R. Part 58, “Environmental Review Procedures for Entities Assuming HUD Environmental Responsibilities” (“HUD Regulations”), for the sole purpose of performing these federal environmental review responsibilities as they relate to the awarding of TCAP funds. II. Directive As the chief elected executive officer of the State, I hereby delegate my responsibilities as Certifying Officer of the Responsible Entity, as defined by the HUD Regulations, to the Executive Director of CHFA or his designee solely as these responsibilities relate to the distribution of TCAP funds. The Executive Director of CHFA or his designee is hereby authorized to do the following: A. Assume the status of Certifying Officer under NEPA and each provision of law designated in the 24 C.F.R. Part 58.5 list of NEPA-related authorities insofar as the provisions of these laws apply to TCAP and HUD responsibilities for environmental review, decision-making, and action that have been assumed by the Responsible Entity, and B. To accept the jurisdiction of the federal courts on behalf of CHFA for the enforcement of these responsibilities. III. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect until modified or rescinded by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this sixth of August, 2009. Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor

full_text: D 2010-002 EXECUTIVE ORDER Directing the streamlining of the Medicaid and Children’s Basic Health Plan (CBHP) Application Process through Data Sharing Agreements among certain State Agencies Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Ritter, Jr., Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing the Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (HCPF), the Department of Revenue (DOR), the Department of Public Health and Environment (DPHE), and the Governor’s Office of Information Technology (OIT) to enter into data sharing agreements for the purpose of electronically verifying citizenship and identity of persons applying for Medicaid and CBHP in compliance with the Deficit Reduction Act (DRA) of 2005. I. Background, Need, and Purpose Section 6036 of the DRA requires states to obtain satisfactory documentary evidence of an applicant’s or client’s citizenship and identity in order to receive Federal Financial Participation (FFP). Effective July 1, 2006, individuals must provide satisfactory documentary evidence of citizenship and identity when initially applying for Medicaid or upon a client’s first Medicaid re- determination. The statute and interim final regulation provide states with guidance on acceptable documentary evidence, including alternative forms not explicitly named in statute. The statute and regulation also give states guidance on the processes that may be used to minimize the administrative burden on states, applicants, and clients. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) have encouraged states to utilize automated matching systems to verify citizenship and identity in order to satisfy these requirements. The Children’s Health Insurance Program Reauthorization Act (CHIPRA) of 2009 extended the citizenship documentation requirements in Medicaid to CBHP effective January 1, 2010. Many national studies have found that the citizenship and identity requirements under the DRA make acquiring and maintaining children’s and families’ coverage more difficult. The new requirements increase the complexity, administrative burden, and costs of enrollment and renewal. As a result, the number of uninsured citizens, as well as the amount of uncompensated care provided by hospitals and other health care providers to low-income individuals, has increased. Executive Order D 2010-002 February 11, 2010 Page 2 of 4 The federal regulations permit states to use a cross-match with state vital statistics agencies to document an individual’s birth record and to match records with other government agencies to establish an individual’s identity and citizenship. These regulations allow states to use information technology to reduce the paperwork burdens that the new citizenship requirement imposes on citizens, current beneficiaries, and state eligibility workers alike. That, in turn, can reduce uninsured and uncompensated care. The Center on Budget and Policy Priorities reported that of all persons eligible for public programs in the State of Colorado, seventy-eight percent of children and forty-three percent of adults between the ages of eighteen and sixty-four were born in Colorado and appear in the state’s vital statistics database. Families report that the administrative burdens to and the costs of acquiring birth certificates prevent them from completing their Medicaid and CHBP applications. Thus, facilitating data matches with vital statistics data could simplify citizenship verification for the majority of applicants. In Colorado, there is a clear need to develop a structured, well-coordinated approach to making the verification process more efficient and effective. In addition to achieving these goals, improving the application process by facilitating direct access to state databases with verifiable information reduces the likelihood of applicants and clients submitting documentation that is not factual or authentic. The availability of electronic data sharing between various State and federal agencies to verify income, citizenship, and identity results in a streamlined process that is beneficial to the applicants applying for Medicaid and CBHP and the citizens of the State of Colorado. The State would greatly benefit from establishing such a partnership of state agencies for this purpose. II. Directives A. The Executive Directors and staff of HCPF, DOR, and DPHE, in collaboration with OIT, shall be responsible for implementing the electronic data sharing of citizenship and identity documentation. B. The initial tasks shall include the following: 1. Convene a committee of relevant state departments to establish priorities, develop strategies, and begin identifying the business requirements and associated costs of implementing electronic data sharing between the state departments. 2. Develop interagency data-sharing agreements to determine what information and how such information shall be shared between HCPF and DPHE and between HCPF and DOR. 3. Pilot the sharing of Vital Statistics electronic data managed by DPHE for twenty medical assistance sites and/or county department of social/human Executive Order D 2010-002 February 11, 2010 Page 3 of 4 services eligibility technicians trained to conduct the application process in the Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS). 4. Pilot the sharing of drivers license-related electronic data managed by DOR with HCPF. 5. Pilot the sharing of vital statistics data with the Driver License System to update its data for individuals with driver licenses and identification cards. III. Deliverables Based on the above outlined directives, the Executive Director of the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing shall deliver a report to the Governor’s Office no later than December 31, 2010, which shall include the following: A. A set of identified priorities and strategies for electronic data sharing; B. An update on the progress made with respect to the pilot data sharing efforts; C. An update on the high level business requirements and associated costs of implementing electronic data sharing on a statewide basis; and D. An update on the status of the interagency agreements between the respective state departments. IV. Staffing and Resources Any of the agencies subject to this directive shall have the power to accept money and in-kind contributions from private entities and persons only to the extent such donations are necessary to cover its expenses. Any money contributed shall be directed to the Office of the Governor and deposited with the Treasurer of the State of Colorado in an account within the Office of the Governor’s budget. Executive Order D 2010-002 February 11, 2010 Page 4 of 4 V. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until modified or rescinded by future Executive Order of the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this eleventh of February, 2010. Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor

full_text: D 2010-011 EXECUTIVE ORDER Rescinding Executive Order D 005 09 Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Ritter, Jr. Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order rescinding Executive Order D 005 09. I. Background and Purpose Beginning early on the morning of March 26, 2009, a blizzard hit the State and impacted traffic safety, including causing the closure of U.S. Highway 36 between Westminster and Boulder and stranding motorists who required rescue. As Governor, I ordered “that $200,000 be transferred from the Major Medical Insurance Fund to the Disaster Emergency Fund.” However, as the situation unfolded, the state response did not require these funds, and the transfer never took place. The presence of a credit, but not a cash transfer, on the balance sheet of the Disaster Emergency Fund now requires resolution. Garcia, Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado and acting temporarily as Governor while Governor John W. Hickenlooper is absent from the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending an earlier declaration of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in Boulder County, Colorado and extending availability of funds and authorization to enter upon land to remove debris. I. Background and Purpose On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. The Fourmile Fire poses an imminent danger to human life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster. In response to this disaster, on September 7, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-012 declaring a disaster emergency. Two days later, on September 9, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-013, reaffirming his disaster declaration and making additional state resources available to support the State's response to the Fourmile Fire. By the time the Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had spread to more than 3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and destroyed 169 homes. With the assistance of Boulder County Emergency Management, the residents have been diligently working to clear land of fire debris. However, the inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term. Once a disaster declaration has been made, state law authorizes the Governor to order the removal or clearance of debris or wreckage from public or private lands through the use of ---PAGE--- "any of the state's instrumentalities" when such debris "may threaten public health or safety or public or private property." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke this authority, the local government must "first present [] an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree[] to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the state, to remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property. The Governor issued Executive Order D 2011-013, Executive Order D 2011-017 and Executive Order D 2011-025, which provided additional thirty-day extensions of authorization to remove debris. The debris removal efforts are still not complete. Indeed, such efforts are not expected to be complete until November 2011. I understand that after September 30, 2011, Boulder County will begin mandatory debris removal procedures on private properties that have not complied with previous debris removal requests and offers of assistance. Thus, I am extending the debris authorization removal authority again. By statute, however, in order to authorize debris removal I must also declare a disaster emergency, the duration of which is limited to thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration. Therefore, with this executive order, I will extend the disaster declaration and debris removal authorization by thirty days, but it is expected that further extensions will be necessary before the work is completed. This thirty day extension is effective upon the date of verbal approval, August 6, 201l. Paragraph I|(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 made $200,000 available for response and recovery efforts. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. The funds from Executive Order D 2010-013, however, are only available through September 9, 2011. In order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, I am extending the availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through September 20, 2012. II. Declaration and Directives In addition to the declarations and directives contained in Executive Orders D 2010-012, D 2010-013, and D 2010-019, Executive Order D 2011-002, Executive Order D 2011-006, Executive Order D 2011-007, Executive Order D 2011-012, Executive Order D 2011-013, Executive Order D 2011-017, and Executive Order D 2011-025, 1 declare and direct, as follows: A. I hereby declare that Fourmile Fire continues to constitute a disaster emergency for purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103. B. I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State, to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile Fire ---PAGE--- from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented to the Governor an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal. C. The $200,000 encumbered pursuant to paragraph II(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 shall remain available through September 30, 2012, for the purposes of the original encumbrance. Specifically, these funds may be used to pay for resources as requested by Boulder County or appropriate state agencies and as approved by the Director of the Division of Emergency Management to assist with government costs incurred during the current disaster emergency by government entities, including costs incurred by non- profit organizations on behalf of government entities. The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate agencies. These funds shall remain available for this purpose through September 20, 2012, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. I. Duration Executive Order D 2010-012 remains in full force and effect as originally promulgated. The funds made available pursuant to paragraph I|(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 shall remain available until September 30, 2012, and in all other respects Executive Order D 2010-013 shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from the date of my verbal order on August 6, 2011, unless extended further by Executive Order. I acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2011-032 November 1, 2011 Page 3 of 3 presented to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal. Garcia, Lieutenant Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issues this Executive Order suspending prescribed or controlled fire by State agencies pending review of agency protocols for prescribed or controlled fire. 1. Background and Purpose Many areas of Colorado have been experiencing above average temperatures and dry conditions. As a result, the National Weather Service has issued a number of Red Flag warnings for the Front Range and other portions of the state. Already this year, Colorado has experienced several wildfires. On March 25, 2012, the Lower North Fork Fire may have been started by a prescribed or controlled fire. As of this issuance of this order, the Lower North Fork Fire had burned approximately several thousand acres, resulted in the deaths of two people, and destroyed several homes. To help respond to the Lower North Fork Fire, on March 27, Lt. Governor Joseph Garcia issued Executive Oder D 2012-005 that activated the National Guard and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. Prescribed or controlled fire is a tool used to reduce the overabundance of vegetation and dense stands of trees—in other words, the fuels-that can lead to intense, catastrophic wildfires. However, it must only be used under the right conditions and under responsible management. As a result, given that a prescribed or controlled fire may have been the cause of the Lower North Fork Fire, the State should suspend further use of this land and fire management tool to make sure that we have the procedures and protocols in place so that these conditions and management requirements are understood and strictly followed. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2012-006 March 28, 2012 Page 2 of 2 HI. This suspension applies to all State lands as well as State agencies that apply prescribed or controlled fire on non-State lands under contracts or agreements with other entities. For purposes of this order, "prescribed or controlled fire" is defined as the controlled application of fire in accordance with a written plan for wildland fuels under specified environmental conditions while following appropriate precautionary measures that ensure that the fire is confined to a predetermined area to accomplish planned fire or land-management objectives. C. For purposes of this order, "prescribed or controlled fire" does not apply to agricultural burning, however, extreme care and caution in agricultural burning is strongly encouraged. full_text: STATE OF COLORADO OFFICE OF THE GOVERNOR D 2014-011 EXECUTIVE ORDER Ordering Funds Transferred to the Resource Mobilization Fund Based on the Imminent Threat of the Impending Wildfire Season 1876 John W. Hickenlooper Governor Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to relevant portions of C.R.S. § 28-3-104 and the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring an imminent threat to the lives and property of the people of the State of Colorado due to the impending wildfire season and ordering transfer of funds into the State's Resource Mobilization Fund to address fires as rapidly as they arise. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire." C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). A. Upcoming Fire Season Wildfires have long posed a risk to the health and safety of the people of Colorado. However, in recent years, the frequency of these fires has increased tremendously. During the 1960s, Colorado saw an average of 457 wildfires that burned 8,170 acres annually, but by the 1990s, these numbers more than doubled to an average of over 1,300 fires burning 22,000 acres annually. By the end of the 2000s, these numbers had again doubled making even a normal fire season very dangerous and costly for our community. Experts also predict that the annual number of fires will continue to increase as drought, beetle kill, and more severe weather conditions increase the likelihood and complexity of wildfires. In 2012 alone Colorado saw 6,459 fires that burned over 250,000 acres, killing six individuals and resulting in $538 million in direct property losses. During 2012 and 2013, the ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2014-011 June 6, 2014 Page 2 of 3 people of Colorado experienced the most destructive fires in the State's recorded history. Experts warn that such destructive fire seasons are likely to become the "new normal" for Colorado. The Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control estimates that, in an average year, large wildfires in Colorado will burn more than 113,000 acres of land and result in more than $41 million in fire suppression expenses. Beyond the direct costs of fighting these fires and the loss of property, the indirect costs to the State are immeasurable but staggering. Indirect costs communities face include loss of tax and business revenue, stalled tourism, and costs associated with resulting health problems and loss of life. One study has indicated that the indirect cost of large wildfires to western states can be up to 30 times greater than the direct suppression costs. There is general consensus among all wildfire experts that the single most effective strategy in containing wildfires is an immediate and rapid response, as this greatly increases the chances that responders will contain fires while they are small. Thus, the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control has identified a primary goal of "keeping fires small." Collaboration between jurisdictions often provides the most effective, if not only way, to respond adequately to wildfires as soon as they are discovered. To assist the State in accomplishing the goal of keeping fires small, the General Assembly in 2013 created a "Resource Mobilization Fund" (RMF). This fund in part provides a mechanism for governmental agencies to be reimbursed for costs accrued when they respond outside of their boundaries to aid neighboring jurisdictions. Mutual assistance from nearby districts is an important element of any immediate response and this fund helps ensure that agencies responding outside of their jurisdictions will be reimbursed for eligible expenses. A rapid and aggressive response by all necessary safety personnel is the best way to keep fires small, save the taxpayer money, and ultimately reduce the risk of loss of life and property. The threat and danger fires pose even in a "normal" fire season is staggering, and it is likely the frequency and scope of wildfires will continue to increase due to changing weather patterns, more severe storms, drought, beetle kill, and increased development. Therefore, I find that the upcoming wildfire season poses an imminent threat to the life and property of the people of the State of Colorado. Accordingly, I direct the State Treasurer to transfer $2,000,000 from the Disaster Emergency Fund to the Resource Mobilization Fund. B. Pipeline Complex Fire By making this transfer, the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety also will have the ability to provide reimbursement to State agencies and jurisdictions for prior incidents. § 24-33.5-705.4(6)(b). As explained below, local responders to the Pipeline Complex Fire from last year will be able to be reimbursed. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2014-011 June 6, 2014 Page 3 of 3 On July 9, 2013 lightning ignited the Crazy Fire and the Pipeline Fire in the area of the Fishers Peak Mesa, approximately five to ten miles southeast of Trinidad in Las Animas County. By July 10, 2013, the Crazy Fire was approximately 40 acres with 90% containment, and the Pipeline Fire was approximately 75 acres with 0% containment. These two fires were named the Pipeline Complex Fire. Local firefighting agencies were the first responders and used local resources to contain the fire. On July 10, 2013, in order to prevent the fire from becoming a disaster emergency and to reduce ultimate costs, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control requested and gained approval of Resource Mobilization as provided in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4. Local firefighting agencies have sought, but not yet received, reimbursement from the State for their initial expenditures related to the Pipeline Complex Fire. By this Executive Order, in addition to making funds available for resource mobilization for this upcoming fire season, the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety is hereby authorized to reimburse local firefighting agencies for expenditures related to the Pipeline Complex Fire from the Resource Mobilization Fund. 1l. Declaration and Directives A. Given Colorado's recent history of devastating fires and the nature of the upcoming wildfire season, I determine that a disaster emergency is imminent pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4.5)(a). I direct the State Treasurer to transfer $2,000,000 from the Disaster Emergency Fund established by C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a) to the Resource Mobilization Fund established by C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(6). B. The Emergency Management Director is hereby authorized to use monies from the Resource Mobilization Fund to provide reimbursement to State agencies for the costs they expended during the Pipeline Complex Fire in accordance with C.R.S. § 24-35-705.4(6)(b). CUTIVI GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of - the Cou Governor ---PAGE--- ---PAGE---
