full_text: D 014 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Energy Performance Contracting to Improve State Facilities Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning energy performance contracting. 1. Background and Purpose Energy performance contracting enables state governments to invest in energy-saving equipment, using future utility cost savings (or avoided costs) to pay for the improvements. A lease-purchase agreement is paid through annually guaranteed cost savings that are realized in utility and operating budgets. Substantial facility improvements can be accomplished in this way while reducing future utility and maintenance costs, mitigating the future risk of volatile utility prices and modernizing state facilities. A number of state agencies and institutions have tested and proven this approach. The potential exists for substantial improvements in the use of utility and operating budgets. Legislation to govern energy performance contracts was adopted in House Bill 1381 in 2001, C.R.S. §§ 24-30-2001 through 24-30-2004 and C.R.S. §§ 24-75-108 and 29-4-729. The Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation and the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs developed procurement and contracting documents, project guidelines, and reporting and tracking procedures for performance contracting projects. I direct all agencies of state government to initiate energy performance contracts where opportunity exists to better utilize utility and operating budgets and to make capital improvements in facilities. To assist agencies in this effort, the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation, in partnership with the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs, offers substantial technical services including project development, engineering review, and project implementation guidance. 2. Directive Each state agency responsible for state-owned facilities shall: a. Investigate the feasibility for an energy performance contract and submit a final feasibility study to the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs by July 1, 2004. The feasibility study will be for a performance contract that is comprehensive in scope to implement a wide range of cost-effective energy-saving projects in all buildings, considering a financing term of 12 years or more to capture substantial avoided costs. Guidelines for the feasibility study are available from the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs. Professional engineering services to complete the study are available at no cost through the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation. b. Issue a Request For Proposal for services by February 2005 and follow- through with implementation through an energy performance contract for all buildings or a manageable portion of buildings, where it is determined that a performance contract is feasible, viable and economically sound. Assistance in developing an RFP is available through the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation, in cooperation with the Department of Personnel &Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs. c. Follow established procedures and re quirements as set by the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs, utilizing approved procurement and contracting documents and following construction project guidelines and documenting and reporting procedures. State Institutions of Higher Education are encouraged to comply with subsections a-c of this section 2. Except in the case of emergency or extenuating circumstances as determined by the Office of State Planning and Budgeting, no Fiscal Year 2005/2006 or future requests for Controlled Maintenance shall be approved by the Office of State Planning and Budgeting (including approvals from the State Buildings and Real Estate Programs and the Colorado Commission of Higher Education) for any department, agency, or institution of the state that has not submitted an energy performance contract feasibility study approved by the Department of Personnel & Administration’s State Buildings and Real Estate Programs. 3. Implementation All departmental and institutional changes necessary to implement this Executive Order shall be made within existing budgetary appropriations. It is the intent of this Executive Order that future utility and operational budgets will be structured so that the annual cost to support a performance contract will be supported by the utility appropriation that would otherwise be granted. 4. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until modified or terminated by further executive order of the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 16th day of July, 2003. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 015 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency and Making Certain Emergency Management Funds Available for Wildfire Suppression Activities Pursuant to the authority vested in the O ffice of the Governor of the State of Colorado and in particular Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2104, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a disaster emergency and making certain funds available from the Emergency Management Fund for wildfire suppression activities. 1. Background and Purpose In 2002, Colorado experienced one of the worst wildfires seasons in state history. Extreme drought conditions and consistently high temperatures created an extremely dangerous fire season. This year, spring precipitation has delayed the fire season, however, the potential for a serious wildfire season remains. The spring precipitation did not eliminate the effects of the recent drought. The Western and southeastern parts of Colorado are still facing drought conditions and the remainder of the state has below average moisture conditions. Recent hot and dry conditions have escalated this risk of wildfires. Since July 8, 2003, numerous wildfires have been ignited throughout the state. The 2002 fire season offered a difficult example that even small brush fires have the potential to develop into massive wildfires that take months to extinguish. These wildfires can cause extensive damage to property and, more importantly, threaten human life. For these reasons, the State of Colorado has advanced an aggressive approach to fighting wildfires. On April 6, 2003, I signed Executive Order D 008 03, which made state disaster funds available to pre-position Single Engine Air Tankers and to staff wildland interface fire engines with the objective of putting out fires while they are still controllable. This plan has been successful. Numerous fires throughout the state have had the potential to cause extensive damage but have been controlled due to responsive and effective firefighting efforts. The State of Colorado must continue to take aggressive measures to control fires during the 2003 wildfire season. Given the return of hot and dry conditions, each fire has the potential to cause widespread damage to property and to threaten human life. As envisioned by the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act of 1992, threats to the public safety of this magnitude confer upon the Governor unique powers and responsibilities. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters. The Act defines disasters as the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire. C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). If the Governor finds that the demands placed upon regularly appropriated funds in coping with a particular disaster are unreasonably great, the Governor may make funds available from the disaster emergency fund. C.R.S. § 24-32-2106(4). Executive Order D 008 03 made extensive resources available to prepare for the 2003 wildfire season. This Executive Order continues the State of Colorado’s aggressive plan to control wildfires by making disaster emergency funds available to vigorously fight wildfires before they burn out of control. Since July 8, 2003, I have determined that six fires constitute disaster emergencies. In each instance, I determined that these fires could pose a threat to property or human life and I immediately made disaster emergency funds available to ensure that proper resources were available to control each of these fires. These fires are: 1) the Campbell Fire located in Park County; 2) the Oso Fire located in Gunnison County; 3) the Brush Mountain Fire located in Garfield County; 4) the Carr Fire located in Garfield County; 5) the Dry Park Fire located in Garfield County; and 6) the Horn Fire located in La Plata County. These fires have burned a total of 6,352 acres, to date. This Executive Order hereby acknowledges my earlier verbal orders declaring each of these fires a disaster emergency and makes disaster emergency funds available to pay for these efforts. 2. Mission A. I hereby declare that the six wildfires described above constituted a disaster emergency for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order the encumbrance of up to $4,000,000 from the State Disaster Emergency Fund to cover costs associated with fighting these fires, as well as future fires that are declared a disaster emergency. These funds shall remain available for this purpose until June 30, 2004. C. The Director of the Colorado Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to coordinate application to the federal government for any reimbursable expenses related to this Executive Order. D. All verbal orders that I issued in regards to these disaster emergencies are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and t h e E x e c u t i v e S e a l o f t h e State of Colorado, this 25th day of July, 2003. B i l l O w e n s G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 016 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Centralized Leasing Procedures Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning centralized leasing and real property acquisition procedures for state departments and institutions. 1. Background and Need Since 1989, the State of Colorado has used a contracted brokerage lease management program to assist state agencies and institutions in their real estate transactions. The Department of Personnel & Administration (DPA) administers this program through the Division of Finance and Procurement, State Buildings and Real Estate Programs Section. The program has improved service to the agencies’ clients, increased staff cost savings, and improved the fit between agency needs and overall state real estate occupancies. DPA has begun to apply comprehensive real estate asset management practices to the state’s diverse portfolio of real estate, including leased assets, however, the current program’s success is constrained. State agencies and institutions commonly pursue their leasing needs independently, resulting in inefficient use of space and inadequate and uncoordinated long term planning. In addition, state staff resources are not sufficient to fully implement comprehensive management across all state agencies and institutions. Current fiscal challenges have highlighted the need for more comprehensive, coordinated planning for space occupancy, particularly within the capitol complex and in the Denver metropolitan area. Ad hoc decisions about occupation of state-owned or leased property neglect opportunities for collocation and cost reduction. A comprehensive real estate management program will ensure optimum use of owned and leased space, and will maximize state expenditures. This Executive Order permits the state to develop and implement a new framework for control and oversight of leasing and other real property acquisition by state agencies and institutions, including development of a new contract for additional tenant brokerage services. 2. Directives and Implementation a. DPA shall issue a new Request for Pr oposals (RFP) for contracted brokerage lease management services for Adams, Arapahoe, Boulder, Broomfield, Denver, Douglas and Jefferson Counties (“Denver metro area”) and other areas of the state as determined by the Executive Director of DPA. DPA shall issue the RFP no later than October 1, 2003, for a contract date commencing no later than January 1, 2004. The RFP shall include provisions for strategic planning services for the capitol complex, the Denver metro area, and other areas identified in the RFP (with completion of a strategic plan due no later than July 1, 2004), buyer/tenant representation services, and lease management functions by the contracted broker. b. Until completion of the strategic plan, executive branch agencies (including higher education institutions) shall not enter into leases for office space or otherwise acquire leased or owned space, including lease renewals, in the Denver metro area or other designated areas unless written authorization is granted by the Governor’s Office of State Planning and Budgeting (OSPB) or the Colorado Commission on Higher Education (CCHE) (in the case of higher education institutions). In the meantime, OSPB, CCHE and DPA shall, in their discretion, make every effort to accommodate space needs that will not compromise efforts for strategic planning or which should be accomplished to maximize market opportunities. c. Representatives from OSPB, CCHE, DPA and the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) shall develop, by January 1, 2004, a centralized framework for a more efficient, effective, and economical space acquisition and leasing program for state agency and institutional space needs. The program shall i) specify the procedures and authority for approval of all executive branch and higher education space requests, ii) require DPA or its designees to negotiate all lease agreements on behalf of state agencies and institutions and iii) define required documentation and justification for space acquisition requests. DPA, in coordination with CCHE and CDOT and subject to approval by OSPB, shall develop policies and procedures to implement this program. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect until further modification or rescission by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 24 th day of August , 2003. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 019 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER Delegation of Authority for the Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and in particular, Art. IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning the delegation of executive authority to the state Adjutant General regarding the operations of the Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit. 1. Background and Mission The United States Army has proposed to establish and fund a new unit assigned to the Colorado National Guard in furtherance of the Ground Based Midcourse Defense System (the “Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit” or “Unit”.) The Unit will employ approximately 75 Colorado Guard members and will have a 24- hour per day, 7- day per week federal mission in support of national defense against ballistic missile attack. The Unit will provide local employment opportunities and will enhance the Colorado’s significant role in United States space missions. Military units of the Colorado National Guard are under the command and control of the Governor of Colorado until and unless federalized, and are available for call-up by the Governor for purposes of State Active Duty. C.R.S. §§ 28-3-104 and 204. The Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit will function under the operational control of the federal active duty Armed Forces, pursuant to 10 U.S.C.S. § 12301(d). Members of the Unit will be ordered to federal active duty only if they consent. For administrative purposes, such as hiring and personnel actions, the Unit members will continue to be governed by the authority of the Colorado National Guard and Colorado law. In order to have effective management and operation of the Unit, it is necessary to promote coordination between the Colorado National Guard and the Army and to ensure that the Unit will not be diverted from its mission. The state Adjutant General serves in the executive branch of the state government as an appointee of the Governor (C.R.S. § 28-3-105) and will be in the best position to make prompt and informed decisions about the Unit. Therefore, it is appropriate to grant to the State Adjutant General the authority to release the Unit from State Active Duty and to consent to federal military active duty in furtherance of this mission pursuant to 10 U.S.C.S. § 12301(d). In addition, the Adjutant General shall be responsible for the formation, activation and operations of this Unit. The Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit will be entirely funded from federal sources, including Colorado National Guard members’ salaries. No costs will be incurred by the State of Colorado. 2. Directive A. I hereby delegate to the state Adjutant General the authority to release the Army Ground-Based Midcourse Defense Unit to the exclusive operational control of the United States Army, and to agree to refrain from calling the Unit for state missions. B. I hereby delegate to the state Adjutant General the authority to consent to federal military active duty of Colorado National Guard members in the Army Ground- Based Midcourse Defense Unit for purposes of this mission. I further delegate to the state Adjutant General the authority to enter into Memoranda of Agreement relating to the formation, activation, and operations of this Unit. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 16th day of September, 2003. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 021 03 EXECUTIVE ORDER DIRECTING EXPENDITURE OF FEDERAL FUNDS PURSUANT TO THE JOBS AND GROWTH TAX RELIEF RECONCILIATION ACT OF 2003 Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning the expenditure of federal funds provided to the State pursuant to the Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003, Public Law 108-27. I. Background and Need The Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003, Public Law 108-27, section 601, (the “Act”) provides temporary fiscal relief to states in fiscal years 2003 and 2004. Colorado received approximately $146.3 million in temporary fiscal relief funds. Under the Act, a state must use the funds to provide essential government services or to cover the costs of certain federal unfunded mandates. In addition, the funds must be used for types of expenditures permitted under the most recently approved budget for the State. As Governor, I have the authority to direct the expenditure of these federal funds. Pursuant to the Act, on June 12, 2003, I certified to the United States Department of the Treasury that the State’s proposed use of the funds would comply with the specified purposes. To date, I have allocated nearly $31 million of these funds for children’s health, education, and important safety projects around the state. It is becoming increasingly evident that the national and Colorado economies are improving and that the State’s revenue outlook is stabilizing. Indeed, the national economy grew at an annual rate of 8.2 percent in the third quarter of 2003, the strongest growth in 20 years and State General Fund revenues came in $78 million ahead of the forecast in FY 2002-03. Given this improvement and stabilization in the State’s revenue stream, it is appropriate to disburse the majority of the remaining funds for essential government services in areas of the budget that address immediate concerns and position the State for improved operations. II. Directive A. I hereby direct the following expenditures of federal funds received by the State pursuant to the Jobs and Growth Tax Relief Reconciliation Act of 2003: 1. $60 million to the Colorado Department of Transportation; 2. $12.5 million to the Jobs for Colorado program; 3. $2.5 million for job training programs; 4. $10 million to the Low Income Energy Assistance Program; 5. $7.5 million for the development of a State Internet Portal; 6. $2 million for dental care for children in the Medicaid and CHP+ program; 7. $1 million to enhance and expand the necessary infrastructure for consumer directed support programs; 8. $2,170,140 for the Colorado Bureau of Investigation to improve the State’s DNA testing program; 9. $704,000 for the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment for an immunization program and for the Ryan White Program; 10. $250,000 for the tuition assistance program at the Colorado National Guard; 11. $1,764,267 to the Department of Corrections to facilitate the expansion of prison beds for female inmates; 12. $50,000 for the Talking Library for the blind and disabled; 13. $1,000,000 to the Department of Human Services for the State Veterans’ Nursing Home; 14. $785,000 to the Department of Agriculture for the State Fair; 15. $5 million for the CoverColorado program; 16. $3.2 million for charter school capital construction; and 17. $879,500 for phase 3 of 4 of the capital construction request at the Forensics unit at the Colorado Mental Health Institute. B. I hereby direct the Office of State Planning and Budgeting to issue instructions regarding the distribution of these funds and to monitor their expenditure. I also designate the Office of State Planning and Budgeting as the final authority for resolution of any issues that may arise during the expenditure or allocation of these funds. III. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 22nd day of December, 2003. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 001 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER DESIGNATING STATE’S PROSECUTOR Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and in particular Colorado Revised Statute § 24-31-101(1)(a), I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order designating Ken Salazar, Attorney General for the State of Colorado, as the State’s prosecutor, to investigate and prosecute criminal or civil matters related to the University of Colorado and its football team and recruiting practices. 1. Background and Purpose In recent months, the University of Colorado has been the subject of intense local and national scrutiny. In particular, questions surround the University’s football program and recruiting activities, stemming from allegations of rape, sexual misconduct, illegal alcohol use, and other unacceptable and illegal conduct. Reported accusations involve multiple law enforcement agencies and jurisdictions. The creation of one statewide investigative entity is necessary to ensure an inclusive and coherent investigation of these serious issues. The State of Colorado is interested in investigating and potentially filing claims related to the alleged activities because the controversy involves a prominent state institution, and because of the need for a statewide entity authorized to thoroughly investigate and resolve the issues in a comprehensive, consistent, and expeditious manner. For these reasons, I am designating the Attorney General to appear for the State of Colorado to investigate, and if necessary, prosecute such matters in the interest of justice. The Attorney General will appoint a task force to assist with his investigation, to include experts from law enforcement agencies and District Attorneys’ offices from various judicial districts. This designation and investigation is not intended to replace the University’s own established and ongoing investigative endeavors. 2. Mission Pursuant to law and this Executive Order, the Attorney General shall conduct a comprehensive investigation of issues and allegations of sexual offenses and other matters concerning the University of Colorado and its football team and recruiting practices. If evidence warrants and if deemed to be in the public interest, the Attorney General may pursue prosecution of such matters, consistent with state law. 3. Directive I hereby appoint Ken Salazar, Attorney General for the State of Colorado, to be the State’s prosecutor and direct him to take all necessary actions to investigate and prosecute, on behalf of the State of Colorado, claims related to the University of Colorado and its football team and recruiting practices. 4. Duration This appointment and this Executive Order shall expire upon completion of the Attorney General’s investigation and prosecution related to the matters herein, unless modified or terminated by Executive Order of the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 27th day of February 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 002 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER PROMOTING COMMUNITY-BASED ALTERNATIVES FOR INDIVIDUALS WITH DISABILITIES Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order to promote community- based alternatives for individuals with disabilities. 1. Background and Need On June 22, 1999, the Supreme Court held that Title II of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) requires states, whenever possible, to place qualified individuals with mental disabilities in community settings rather than in institutions. Olmstead v. L. C., 527 U.S. 581 (1999). The Olmstead ruling specified that states should transition individuals whenever treatment professionals determine that such placement is appropriate, the affected persons do not oppose such placement, and the state can reasonably accommodate the placement, taking into account the resources available to the state and the needs of others with disabilities. In June 2001, President Bush reinforced the Olmstead decision by signing an Executive Order promoting community-based alternatives, rather than institutions, for individuals with disabilities. Colorado has long been a national leader in building care systems that focus on increased access to services in the least restrictive environments. We have proven that funds can be efficiently directed toward programs for improved community-based services. We are engaged in a stakeholder process addressing the issues involved with transitioning appropriate persons with disabilities to increasingly integrated services. This Executive Order is intended to encourage and direct changes in our programs and policy that will improve our ability to provide community-based alternatives for individuals with disabilities and will be consistent with the requirements of the Olmstead decision and the President’s Executive Order. 2. Directive The Colorado Department of Human Services and Department of Health Care Policy and Financing shall evaluate the policies, programs, statutes, and regulations of their respective agencies to determine whether any should be revised or modified to improve the availability of community-based services for qualified individuals with disabilities. The review shall focus on identifying affected populations, improving the flow of information about supports in the community, and removing barriers that impede opportunities for community placement. The review should ensure the involvement of consumers, advocacy organizations, providers, and relevant agency representatives. The Departments of Human Services and Health Care Policy and Financing shall provide a status report of their progress on this directive to the Office of State Planning and Budgeting on a semi- annual basis, by June 30 and December 31 of each year. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until December 31, 2006. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 15th day of March 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 004 04 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to a Wildfire in Larimer County Pursuant to the authority vested in th e Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and pursuant to the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, §24-32-2100 et seq., C.R.S., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency. 1. Background and Need. On March 31, 2004, a small fire in Larimer County quickly escalated into a major wildfire due to dry conditions and heavy winds. As of this time, the “Picnic Rock Fire” has burned approximately 6,000 acres, destroyed one home, and is threatening an additional 100 homes. Residents living in these homes have been evacuated. Unseasonably warm, dry and windy weather has caused this fire to spread in a rapid and erratic manner. The time frame in which this fire is contained is largely dependent on weather conditions. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire…” C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). As detailed above, this wildfire poses an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore, I find that it constitutes a disaster for the purposes of the Act. When the life or property of its citizens is at risk, the State of Colorado will use every resource at its disposal to end that threat. I have ordered the immediate use of state funds and state resources to contain and extinguish this wildfire in the shortest possible timeframe. 2. Mission and Scope. A. I hereby declare that the Picnic Rock Fi re constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order the encumbrance of $2.2 million from the State Disaster Emergency Fund to finance fire suppression activities. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for six months from the date of this Executive Order. C. The Director of the Colorado Offi ce of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to coordinate application to the federal government for any funds for public assistance disaster relief and for other funding related to the disaster emergency. D. All verbal orders that I issued in re gard to this disaster emergency, including my verbal disaster emergency declaration on April 1, 2004, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 2nd day of April, 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 005 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER Delegation of Authority for Colorado National Guard Training Activities Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and in particular, Art IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution, I Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order regarding calling members of Colorado National Guard to State Active Duty for training purposes. 1. Background The Colorado National Guard plays a critical role in the state’s emergency preparedness and disaster response plans. The Colorado National Guard is a supporting agency for nearly every state emergency function including wildfire suppression activities and Homeland Security and Homeland Defense plans. Members of the Colorado National Guard must receive specialized training to be prepared for these duties. Military units of the Colorado National Guard are under the command and control of the Governor of Colorado until and unless federalized, and are available for call-up to State Active Duty only by the Governor. It is inefficient for the Governor to call-up members of the Colorado National Guard for every training exercise. I have determined that the state Adjutant General is in the best position to determine when members of the Colorado National Guard should be called to State Active Duty for training purposes. By this Executive Order, I delegate this limited function to the Adjutant General. 2. Directive A. I hereby delegate to the state Adju tant General the authority to call-up members of the Colorado National Guard for State Active Duty for training purposes. B. Members of the Colorado National Guard who are called to State Active Duty under this process shall be subject to military chain of command and the authority of the Colorado Code of Military Justice. C. This delegation does not extend to the call-up of the National Guard for state missions and this Executive Order does not authorize the use of state emergency funds. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in full force and effect unless or until modified or rescinded by future Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 26th day of May, 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 006 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat of Wildfires Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2101 et seq., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order making certain funds available from the Emergency Management Fund for wildfire preparation and suppression activities. 1. Background and Purpose. On March 24, 2004, I signed Executive Order D 003 04, making disaster emergency funds available to prepare for the 2004 wildfire season. The majority of these funds are being used to strategically pre-position 3 Single Engine Air Tankers (SEATS) in Colorado. As set forth in my previous Executive Order, pre-positioning air tankers has proven to be an extremely effective tool for extinguishing wildfires before they grow out of control. On May 10, 2004, the United States Department of Interior and the U.S. Forest Service grounded all heavy firefighting air tankers. This decision was based upon a recent National Transportation Safety Board report that questioned the safety of these planes. Although the federal government is providing replacement air resources on a regional national basis, Colorado needs to ensure that adequate air resources are exclusively dedicated to fires within this state. By this Executive Order, I am making funds immediately available for the state to contract additional private air resources to suppress wildfires within the State of Colorado during the 2004 wildfire season. 2. Directive. I hereby declare that the imminent threat of wildfires constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order $1.3 million in disaster emergency funds be made immediately available to contract two additional Single Engine Air Tankers and one helicopter specifically equipped to fight wildfires. These funds shall remain available for this purpose until December 31, 2004. 3. Duration. This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 27th day of May, 2004. B i l l O w e n s G o v e r n o r

full_text: D 011 04 EXECUTIVE ORDER NATIONAL INCIDENT MANAGEMENT SYSTEM Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning the designation of the National Incident Management System (“NIMS”) as the basis for all incident management in the State of Colorado. 1. Background and Need The President of the United States, in Homeland Security Directive (HSPD)-5, directed the Secretary of the United States Department of Homeland Security to develop and administer a national incident management system, which would provide a consistent nationwide approach for Federal, State, local, and tribal governments to work together more effectively and efficiently to prevent, prepare for, respond to, and recover from domestic incidents, regardless of cause, size, or complexity. In addition, the National Commission on Terrorist Attacks (9-11 Commission) recommended adoption of a standardized Incident Command System. The collective input and guidance from all Federal, State, local, and tribal homeland security partners has been, and will continue to be, vital to the development, effective implementation and utilization of a comprehensive NIMS. It is necessary and desirable that all Federal, State, local, and tribal emergency agencies and personnel coordinate their efforts to effectively and efficiently provide the highest levels of incident management. In order to facilitate the most efficient and effective incident management it is critical that Federal, State, local, and tribal organizations utilize standardized terminology, standardized organizational structures, interoperable communications, consolidated action plans, unified command structures, uniform personnel qualification standards, uniform standards for planning, training, and exercising, comprehensive resource management, and designated incident facilities during emergencies or disasters. The NIMS standardized procedures for managing personnel, communications, facilities and resources will improve Colorado’s ability to utilize federal funding to enhance local and state agency readiness, maintain first responder safety, and streamline incident management processes. Furthermore, the Incident Command System components of NIMS are already an integral part of various incident management activities throughout the State, including current emergency management training programs. 2. Directive I hereby establish the National Incident Management System as the State standard for incident management. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect until further modification or rescission by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 6 th day of December, 2004. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 004 05 EXECUTIVE ORDER OFFICE OF THE COLORADO BENEFITS MANAGEMENT SYSTEM Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order establishing the Governor’s Office of the Colorado Benefits Management System. 1. Background and Need The Colorado Benefits Management System (“CBMS”) is a state-of-the-art eligibility and payment system for issuing benefits to clients across Colorado for a variety of social service programs administered by counties and select medical assistance sites. The Colorado Department of Human Services (“CDHS”) and the Colorado Department of Health Care Policy and Financing (“HCPF”) began developing CBMS in 1995 after receiving approval from the Colorado General Assembly and federal agencies. Increasingly complex programs and regulations drove the need for CBMS amid concerns that Colorado could no longer rely upon outdated technology and inconsistent methods of determining eligibility to state and federal programs. CBMS replaced six existing computer systems with one unified system for collecting data, establishing eligibility, and processing payments. CBMS was envisioned to improve access to public assistance and medical benefits by integrating the functions of the existing automated systems, providing one-stop shopping for clients, permitting faster eligibility determinations, and providing increased accuracy and consistency in eligibility determinations and benefit calculations statewide. CBMS is a joint state and local government project that provides a single automated system to support benefits issuance and reporting for 36 public assistance programs. These programs annually distribute over $2 billion in benefits, processing over 380,000 cases. While most components of CBMS are functioning correctly, there are some remaining operating problems that must be resolved. In March 2005, I decided to obtain a third party independent verification and validation of the system in order to address remaining problems. Deloitte Consulting recently completed the independent review and provided recommendations for improving the operation and efficiency of CMBS. The number one recommendation was to establish a single executive branch entity to oversee the system. I am implementing this regulation by the establishment of this Office of the Colorado Benefits Management System (“CBMS Office”), and empowering the CBMS Office to review and, if appropriate, implement the remaining recommendations from Deloitte, and to have continuous oversight of the management and operations of CBMS. 2. Mission and Scope The CBMS Office shall be accountable for the overall control of CBMS from a direction, planning, management, and delivery perspective. It shall provide common oversight and coordination of the state management of CBMS. The Director of the CBMS Office will be an employee of the Office of the Governor and will serve at the pleasure of the Governor. 3. Directive The Governor’s Office of the Colorado Benefits Management System is hereby established. CDHS and HCPF shall provide staff assistance as needed to facilitate the transition of functions from those state agencies to the CBMS Office. 4. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 27 th day of May, 2005. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 006 05 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to a Wildfire in Pueblo and Custer Counties and Ordering to State Active Duty Certain Elements of the Colorado National Guard Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and pursuant to the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, §24-32-2100 et seq., C.R.S., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency. 1. Background and Need. On Wednesday, July 7, 2005, a lightning sparked fire originated in southern Colorado. Due to dry conditions and heavy winds, this fire quickly escalated into a major wildfire in Pueblo and Custer Counties. As of this time, the “Mason Fire” has burned approximately 12,500 acres. It is estimated that 750 structures are threatened by the wildfire and over 5,000 people have been evacuated from their homes. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire…” C.R.S. § 24-32- 2103(1.5). The Mason Fire poses an imminent danger to life and property and, therefore, I find that it constitutes a state disaster emergency. In response, I have encumbered state funds and directed the use of state resources to contain and extinguish this wildfire in the shortest possible timeframe. I have directed the Colorado State Forest Service and its wildfire experts to provide assistance in combating this fire. In addition, the state has made Single Engine Air Tankers, National Guard Helicopters, ground vehicles, and fire crews available to assist in this effort. The State of Colorado will use every resource at its disposal when the life or property of its citizens is at risk. 2. Mission and Scope. A. I hereby declare that the Mason Fire constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order the encumbrance of $2 million from the State Disaster Emergency Fund to finance fire suppression activities. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for nine months from the date of this Executive Order. C. The Director of the Colorado Office of Emergency Management and the Colorado State Forest Service is hereby authorized and directed to coordinate application to the federal government for funds available to individuals affected by this disaster, federal funds available for reimbursement, and for any other funds available related to this disaster emergency. D. All verbal orders made by the Governor and issued in regard to this disaster emergency are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 14th day of July, 2005. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: D 005 05 EXECUTIVE ORDER GREENING OF STATE GOVERNMENT Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order concerning enhancing the efficiency and greening of state government. 1. Background and Need State government needs to operate as efficiently as possible, but at the same time it is important to set an example through efforts to reduce the use of limited resources, increase the cost- effectiveness of state government, and improve Colorado’s environment and the health of our children and future generations. Accordingly, the State of Colorado is committed to business practices that contribute to the mutually compatible goals of economic vitality, a healthy environment and strong communities. The State has already taken significant steps in this direction, particularly under Executive Order D 014 03, Energy Performance Contracting to Improve State Facilities. The Department of Corrections through its Energy Management Program avoids $1.8 million in annual costs (10 percent of its utility budget) and is planning additional facility improvements that could result in avoided annual costs exceeding $1 million. The Department of Human Services through its aggressive program to manage its $5.3 million annual utility budget achieved a 10 percent level of cost avoidance and is implementing projects through performance contracts that will avoid an additional $1,000,000 in annual utility costs. The Department of Personnel and Administration, with the Judicial Department and the Department of Labor & Employment, is using performance contracting for a large-scale, comprehensive effort that captures $800,000 in annual reductions to pay for $14 million in facility upgrades. Other state agencies including the Department of Military Affairs, Colorado School for the Deaf and the Blind, Department of Public Health and Environment, and Department of Natural Resources are implementing similar projects. Within state government, such sustainable practices require decisions based on a systematic evaluation of the costs and long-term impacts of an activity or product on health and safety, communities, and the environment and economy of the State of Colorado. State agencies, through changes in daily operations, ongoing programs, and long-range planning, are able to simultaneously have a significant positive impact on the environment, economic efficiency of state government, and the character of our communities. Government can also foster markets for emerging environmental technologies and products. Finally, state government can be a model for environmental leadership by implementing pollution prevention and resource conservation programs that not only enhance environmental protection, but also save taxpayers’ money through reduced costs, including reduced material costs, waste disposal costs and utility bills. The most effective manner for state government to implement such programs is through the establishment of systems and procedures to evaluate costs and manage environmental impacts. This system should be developed and implemented consistently across state government with the assistance of the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation, Department of Public Health and Environment and Department of Personnel and Administration. 2. Directive A. I hereby direct the Executive Directors of all state agencies and departments to evaluate their current business operations in accordance with the goals of this Order and develop and implement policies and procedures to promote environmentally sustainable and economically efficient practices, including, but not limited to: i. Adopting the United States Green Buildi ngs Council’s Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design Green Building Rating System for Existing Buildings (LEED-EB) in operating, maintaining and managing existing buildings, to the extent applicable and practicable. ii. Incorporating LEED for New Construction (LEED-NC) practices to design energy and resource efficient new buildings, to the extent that this is deemed cost- effective. iii. Initiating an energy management program to monitor and manage utility usage and costs, as resources become available. B. I hereby direct the Executive Directors of the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation, Department of Public Health and Environment, and Department of Personnel and Administration, to establish a Colorado Greening Government Coordinating Council (Council) to include representatives from each state agency and department. C. I hereby direct the Council to develop, implement, and augment programs, plans and policies that save money, prevent pollution and conserve natural resources throughout state government management and operations, including but not limited to source and waste reduction, energy efficiency, water conservation, recycling, fleet operations, environmental preferable purchasing, and establishing state-wide goals to save taxpayers’ money and reduce environmental impacts. D. I hereby direct State agencies and departments to provide all reasonable assistance and cooperation requested by the Council for the purpose of carrying out this order. E. I hereby direct each State agency or department to annually submit to the Council a list of all projects implemented in accordance with this Executive Order in the previous calendar year and the resultant environmental benefits and cost savings. To assist agencies in this effort, the Governor’s Office of Energy Management and Conservation offers technical services to all State departments and agencies. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 15 th day of July, 2005. Bill Owens G o v e r n o r

full_text: STATE OF COLORADO D 008 05 EXECUTIVE ORDER Calling Certain Elements of the Colorado National Guard to Active Duty to Assist with Emergency Response Efforts Related to Hurricane Katrina Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution, and Sections 28-3-104 and 24-32-2100 et seq. of the Colorado Revised Statutes, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order calling certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to state active duty and implement the Emergency Management Assistance Compact to assist the affected states with emergency response efforts related to Hurricane Katrina. 1. Background and Need The Southeastern United States has recently suffered one of the worst natural disasters in our nation’s history. Hurricane Katrina moved through this region leaving destructive effects in its path. The number of lives lost and property damaged is devastating. The State of Louisiana appears to have endured the most damage through this disaster. President Bush has implemented decisive and coordinated federal action to respond to this disaster emergency. Each state must now contribute whatever resources they have to assist in this disaster response effort. As a party to the Emergency Management Assistance Compact, § 24-60-2901 et seq., the State of Colorado is able to provide assistance to states enduring a disaster emergency. By this Order, I call certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to active duty and direct the Colorado National Guard to assist states affected by Hurricane Katrina. To further expedite this assistance, the State of Colorado has agreed to direct specific support to the state most significantly affected by this disaster. Louisiana Governor Kathleen Blanco and I have signed a Memorandum of Understanding which will structure the immediate deployment of Colorado personnel and equipment to assist in the emergency response efforts in Louisiana. EXECUTIVE CHAMBERS 136 State Capitol Denver, CO 80203 - 1792 Phone (303) 866-2471 ____________________ Bill Owens Governor 2. Mission and Scope A. Pursuant to § 28-3-104, C.R.S., as commander in chief of military forces, I hereby employ and call to active duty certain elements of the Colorado National Guard and implement the Emergency Management Assistance Compact. The State of Colorado shall provide support personnel and resources to assist in emergency response efforts related to Hurricane Katrina. This assistance shall be provided to states that qualify for such assistance under § 24-60-2901, et seq., C.R.S. B. Assistance provided by the State of Colorado to the State of Louisiana shall be further guided by the Memorandum of Understanding between the State of Louisiana and the State of Colorado, and executed by Governor Blanco of Louisiana and myself on September 1, 2005. C. I hereby direct Adjutant General Mason Whitney of the Colorado National Guard to immediately coordinate and execute all directives issued by this Executive Order. D. All verbal orders that I issued in regards to this Order are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 3. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. Given under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this 1st day of September, 2005. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: STATE OF COLORADO D 010 05 EXECUTIVE ORDER Directing State Agencies to Prepare Temporary Housing For Evacuees Displaced by Hurricane Katrina Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to § 24-32-2101 et seq. and § 24-60-2901 et seq. of the Colorado Revised Statutes, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing certain state agencies to take action to prepare temporary housing for evacuees displaced by Hurricane Katrina. 1. Evacuees are being taken to safe locations in the region but these cities have exceeded their capacity and capability to provide effective shelter and assistance to displaced citizens. The State of Colorado must provide immediate assistance to address this situation. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act bestows special powers to the Governor during periods of a disaster emergency. full_text: STATE OF COLORADO D 001 06 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to a Wildfire in Las Animas and Huerfano Counties Pursuant to the authority vested in th e Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, and pursuant to the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, §24-32-2100 et seq., C.R.S., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency. 1. Background and Need. On Saturday, January 7, 2006, a fire ignited in southern Colorado. Due to dry conditions and heavy winds, this fire quickly escalated into a major wildfire in Las Animas and Huerfano Counties. As of this time, the “Mauricio Canyon Fire” has burned approximately 6,000 acres and destroyed at least five homes. Hundreds of people have been evacuated from their homes and approximately one thousand more residents have been warned to prepare to evacuate if the fire continues to spread. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire…” C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). On January 8, 2006, I issued a verbal order declaring that the Mauricio Canyon Fire constituted a disaster for the purposes of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act. In response, I have encumbered state funds and directed the use of state resources to contain and extinguish this wildfire in the shortest possible timeframe. I have directed the Colorado State Forest Service and its wildfire experts to provide assistance in combating this fire. In addition, the state has made single engine air tankers, National Guard helicopters, ground vehicles, and fire crews available to assist in this effort. The State of EXECUTIVE CHAMBERS 136 State Capitol Denver, CO 80203 - 1792 Phone (303) 866-2471 ____________________ Bill Owens Governor Colorado will use every resource at its disposal when the life or property of its citizens is at risk. 2. Mission and Scope. A. I hereby declare that the Mauricio Canyon Fire constitutes a disaster for purposes of C.R.S. §24-32-2103. B. The Director of the Colorado Office of Emergency Management and the Colorado State Forest Service is hereby authorized and directed to coordinate application to the federal government for funds available to individuals affected by this disaster, federal funds available for reimbursement, and for any other funds available related to this disaster emergency. C. All verbal orders I issu ed in regard to this disaster emergency, including my disaster emergency declaration on January 8, 2006, are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 3. Funding Directive A. It is the policy of the state that funds shall always be available to meet disaster emergencies. C.R.S. § 24-32-2106(1). Because the Disaster Emergency fund balance is $360,000, it is necessary to transfer funds from the TABOR Emergency Reserve. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106(4), I hereby order the transfer of $240,000 from the TABOR Emergency Reserve into the Disaster Emergency fund. The Director of the Office of State Planning and Budgeting shall determine which particular TABOR Emergency Reserve accounts shall be deducted. B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order the encumbrance of $600,000 from the State Disaster Emergency Fund to finance fire suppression activities. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for nine months from the date of this Executive Order. 4. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from its date of signature unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 9th day of January, 2006. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: STATE OF COLORADO D 002 06 EXECUTIVE ORDER Open Burning Ban on State Lands Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and Colorado Revised Statute § 23-30-308, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing state agencies to prohibit open fires on certain state lands. 1. Background & Need. Unseasonably high temperatures and dry conditions have resulted in high fire danger in certain parts of Colorado. Already this year, Colorado has experienced several fires, including the Mauricio Canyon Fire, which burned over 6,000 acres of land and the fire near Carter Lake in Larimer County, which burned over 300 acres of land. Given the conditions of extreme fire danger in certain parts of the state, additional measures are warranted to respond to this risk and restrict human activities that have the potential of igniting a wildfire on our state lands. The Colorado State Forest Service has advised me that the fire risk is limited to lower elevations that have not received adequate precipitation. Therefore, this Executive Order bans open burning on all state lands below and elevation of 8,000 feet. 2. Directive. full_text: STATE OF COLORADO EXECUTIVE CHAMBERS 136 State Capitol Denver, CO 80203 - 1792 Phone (303) 866-2471 ____________________ Bill Owens Governor D 003 06 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Imminent Threat of Wildfires Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, Colorado Revised Statute § 24-32-2101 et seq., I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order making certain funds available from the Disaster Emergency Fund for wildfire preparation and suppression activities. 1. Background & Need. For the past four years, the State has focused resources on mitigating wildfire risks and building the capability to contain wildfires before they become uncontrollable. Accordingly, I have proactively utilized state disaster emergency funds to pre-position wildfire-fighting resources for the fire season. Ordinarily, we begin this pre-positioning process in the spring. However, already this year, Colorado has experienced several fires, including the Mauricio Canyon Fire, which burned over 6,000 acres of land and the fire near Carter Lake in Larimer County, which burned over 300 acres of land. Given the conditions of extreme fire danger, it is necessary to make funds available to address immediate risks due to unseasonably dry weather. As envisioned by the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act (the “Act”), threats to the public safety of this magnitude confer upon the Governor unique powers and responsibilities. As Governor, I am responsible for meeting dangers to our state presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-32-2104(1). The Act defines disasters as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire . . . .” C.R.S. § 24-32-2103(1.5). The purpose of the Act is to reduce the vulnerability of injury to the people of Colorado and damage to property located within the state and provide for coordination of activities relating to disaster prevention, preparedness and response by the state. C.R.S. § 24-32-2102(1)(a) and (f). In accordance with the Act, this Executive Order makes certain funds available for wildfire mitigation and preparedness activities, including contracting of Single Engine Air Tankers, call as needed helicopters specifically equipped to fight wildfires, staffing additional wildland interface fire engines, employment of wildfire hand crews, and to provide for other preparedness and mitigation resources. 2. Directive. A. In accordance with §24-32-2102 and in order to reduce the vulnerability of injury to the people of Colorado and damage to property located within the state and provide for coordination of activities relating to disaster prevention, preparedness and response by the state, I hereby declare that the imminent threat of wildfires constitutes a disaster, as defined by C.R.S. § 24-32-2103. B. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-32-2106, I order $358,000 in disaster emergency funds be available for the expenses incurred during the period of this Executive Order. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for nine months from the date of this Executive Order. C. The disaster emergency funds authorized by this Executive Order shall be made available to the State Forest Service for wildfire preparedness and mitigation activities. D. The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to coordinate application to the federal government for any funds for public assistance disaster relief and for other funding related to the disaster emergency. 3. Duration. This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from the date of its execution unless extended by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 7th day of February, 2006. Bill Owens Governor

full_text: STATE OF COLORADO EXECUTIVE CHAMBERS 136 State Capitol Denver, CO 80203 - 1792 Phone (303) 866-2471 ____________________ Bill Owens Governor D 006 06 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Directing Agencies of State Government to Continue Participating in the Colorado Statewide Multi-Use Network Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order directing agencies of state government to continue participating in the Colorado Statewide Multi-Use Network. 1. Background and Purpose Integration of Colorado's telecommunications infrastructure provides Colorado's state and local governments, educators, businesses, and citizens with connections between and among institutions of higher education, school districts, public libraries, public hospitals, courts, and government offices. This integration is achieved through planned and coordinated purchases of telecommunications technology by all state departments, agencies, and institutions, including higher education. These coordinated purchases allow the state to take advantage of technologies of scale and assume the role of an anchor tenant in encouraging private sector investment in the infrastructure adequate to provide state-of-the-art telecommunications throughout the state. The resulting investment will lead to increased efficiency and greater economic development. The Multi-Use Network Task Force created by Executive Order B 02 01 completed and published a “Strategic Plan for a Statewide Telecommunications Infrastructure.” The Strategic Plan called for the design and development of a private sector owned and operated network in which the State of Colorado would act as the anchor tenant. In June of 2000, the Department of Personnel & Administration put the plan into effect through a public-private partnership with Qwest Communications creating the Multi-Use Network (“MNT”). The original contractual term between the State of Colorado and Qwest Communications for services provided by this MNT network was through June of 2005 and was subsequently extended through June of 2010. In addition to the economic benefits, use of the MNT will transform government service. The MNT provides the high-speed Internet connections that make "e-government" possible. This process grants citizens with the convenience of filling out forms and obtaining licenses and permits over the internet. Once the MNT is complete, on-line applications will be accessible to the vast majority of Colorado citizens, making State government more efficient and user friendly. 2. Participation Extended Participation in the State of Colorado Multi-Use Network by all state departments, agencies and institutions, including higher education, is extended through the duration of this Order. 3. Directive A. To achieve the desired benefits in efficiency, economies of scale, and economic development, all state departments, agencies and institutions, including higher education shall: i. ii. iii. i. ii. Continue the migration of telecommunication networks to the Multi-Use Network and cease operation of and any new development of disparate telecommunication networks. Continue conversion of network traffic to the Multi-Use Network in a timely manner according to Private Partner(s) and Department of Personnel & Administration established processes. Provide timely information requested by the Department of Personnel & Administration to aggregate statewide telecommunications technology purchasing. B. The Department of Personnel & Administration shall: Implement and operate the statewide Multi-Use Network in partnership with its public/private partner(s). Maintain a central database and clearinghouse for current telecommunications standards that may be established and for other information that may be helpful to the managers of all state departments, institutions, and agencies, including higher education, in the use and purchase of telecommunications technologies. iii. iv. v. vi. vii. viii. 4. Ensure the aggregation of the state's purchases for telecommunications services. Promote standards for the compatibility of equipment and software among state departments, agencies, and institutions, including higher education, to facilitate the sharing of information. Monitor the activities and progress of the state's private partner(s) to ensure that the contractual terms of the public/private partnership are fulfilled. Report periodically to the Governor on progress toward the goals outlined above. Engage other departments, agencies and institutions in supportive roles in the process, as appropriate. Coordinate with other public entities to achieve the overall goals of this Executive Order. Past Executive Order Superseded and Replaced This Executive Order shall repeal and replace all previous executive orders pertaining to the Multi-Use Network Task Force, and specifically Executive Order B 02 01. 5. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect until modified or rescinded by further executive order of the Governor. full_text: STATE OF COLORADO EXECUTIVE CHAMBERS 136 State Capitol Denver, CO 80203 - 1792 Phone (303) 866-2471 ____________________ Bill Owens Governor D 007 06 E X E C U T I V E O R D E R Calling Certain Elements of the Colorado National Guard to State Active Duty for the Purpose of Force Protection Pursuant to the authority vested in the Office of the Governor of the State of Colorado, I, Bill Owens, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order calling certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to state active duty. 1. Background and Need The Colorado National Guard plays a critical role in the state’s emergency preparedness and protection. The Colorado National Guard is a supporting agency for nearly every state emergency function including Homeland Security and Homeland Defense plans. Based on the on-going global war on terrorism and continued terrorist activity, a threat continues to exist against certain targets throughout the country. These targets vary widely in nature and purpose, but include military installations and other critical infrastructure. Shortly after the terrorist attacks on September 11, 2001, the Secretary of Defense made resources and funding available to the Colorado National Guard to protect critical installations. Members of the Colorado National Guard have been actively protecting personnel at the critical installments since that time. In order to access this federal funding, the Governor must call the members of the National Guard into State Active Duty. Military units of the Colorado National Guard are under the command and control of the Governor of Colorado until and unless federalized, and are available for call-up to State Active Duty only by the Governor. In this Order, I call certain elements of the Colorado National Guard to active duty. The Colorado National Guard will immediately deploy armed military personnel to protect critical National Guard installations for the purpose of protecting personnel. 2. Mission and Scope A. Execution of this Order shall be furt her guided by the Cooperative Agreement and appendices set forth between National Guard Bureau and the State of Colorado. B. Personnel performing duties pursuant to this Executive Order will continue to attend their regularly scheduled monthly drills, annual training, and other military training in support of their unit of assignment and the federal government. C. Total expenditure for this Order will not exceed the total funds received for this purpose by the State of Colorado from the National Guard Bureau. D. Personnel performing this duty are subject to federal mobilization with their unit of assignment. E. Personnel performing this duty are ordere d to take measures consistent with minimum necessary force to protect the lives of personnel within the boundaries of Colorado National Guard facilities. The range of necessary force includes lethal force as a last resort. 3. Directive A. Pursuant to § 28-3-104, C.R.S., as co mmander-in-chief of military forces, I hereby employ and call to state active duty certain elements of the Colorado National Guard for the purpose of safeguarding personnel working at critical Colorado National Guard facilities. B. I hereby direct The Adjutant Gene ral of the Colorado National Guard to immediately coordinate and execute all directives issued by this Executive Order. C. All verbal orders that I issued in regards to this Order are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. 4. Duration This Executive Order shall expire on the 30th day of September 2006. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this 24th day of March, 2006. Bill Owens Governor
