Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order extending an earlier declaration of a state of disaster emergency due to the wildfire in Boulder County, Colorado and extending availability of funds and authorization to enter upon land to remove debris. Background and Purpose On Monday, September 6, 2010, a wildfire ("Fourmile Fire") broke out in Fourmile Canyon, approximately 12 miles northwest of Boulder, Colorado. The Fourmile Fire poses an imminent danger to human life and property and, therefore, constitutes a disaster. In response to this disaster, on September 7, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-012 declaring a disaster emergency. Two days later, on September 9, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-013, reaffirming his disaster declaration and making additional state resources available to support the State's response to the Fourmile Fire. By the time the Fourmile Fire was extinguished on September 14, 2010, the fire had spread to more than 3,000 acres, forced the evacuation of more than 3,000 residents, and destroyed 169 homes. With the assistance of Boulder County Emergency Management, the residents have been diligently working to clear land of fire debris. However, the inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term. Once a disaster declaration has been made, state law authorizes the Governor to order the removal or clearance of debris or wreckage from public or private lands through the use of "any of the state's instrumentalities" when such debris "may threaten public health or safety or public or private property." See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2011-012 April 7, 2011 Page 2 of 3 this authority, the local government must "first present[] an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree[] to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32- 2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the state, to remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property. On March 8, 2011, I issued Executive Order D 2011-007, which once again provided 30 additional days of authorization to remove debris. Although that executive order expires today, the debris removal efforts are not complete. Indeed, such efforts are not expected to be complete until sometime in the spring. Thus, I am extending the debris authorization removal authority. By statute, however, in order to authorize debris removal I must also declare a disaster emergency, the duration of which is limited to thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration. Therefore, with the executive order, I will extend the disaster declaration and debris removal authorization by thirty days, but it expected that several further extensions will be necessary before the work is completed. Paragraph II(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 made $200,000 available for response and recovery efforts. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. The funds from Executive Order D 2010-2013, however, are only available through September 9, 2011. In order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, I am extending the availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through September 20, 2012. II. Declaration and Directives In addition to the declarations and directives contained in Executive Orders D 2010-012, D 2010-013, 2010-019, Executive Order D 2011-002, Executive Order D 2011-006, and Executive Order D 2011-007, I declare and direct, as follows: A. I hereby declare that Fourmile Fire continues to constitutes a disaster emergency for purposes of C.R.S. § 24-32-2103. B. I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State, to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile Fire from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2011-012 April 7, 2011 Page 3 of 3 C. The $200,000 encumbered pursuant to paragraph II(B) of Executive Order D 2010-013 shall remain available through September 30, 2012 for the purposes of the original encumbrance. Specifically, these funds may be used to pay for resources as requested by Boulder County or appropriate state agencies and as approved by the Director of the Division of Emergency Management to assist with government costs incurred during the current disaster emergency by government entities, including costs incurred by non-profit organizations on behalf of government entities. The Director of the Colorado Division of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate agencies. These funds shall remain available for this purpose through September 20, 2012, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. Ill. Duration Executive Order D 2010-012 remains in full force and effect as originally promulgated. The funds made available pursuant to paragraph II(B) of D 2010-013 shall remain available until September 30, 2012, and in all other respects Executive Order D 2010-013 shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from its date of signature unless extended further by Executive Order. However, the inability to identify, contact, or obtain the consent of some private landowners has hampered Boulder County's ability to remove some of the debris left by the fire. This remaining debris, some of which may contain hazardous materials, poses a threat to public health and safety if not removed and properly disposed of in the near-term. See C.R.S. § 24-32-2505(1)(a). In order to invoke this authority, the local government must "first present|] an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, first agree|| to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal." See C.R.S. § 24-32-- 2505(2). On October 7, 2010, Boulder County provided the state with the required authorization and indemnification. Therefore, on December 8, 2010, Governor Ritter issued Executive Order D 2010-019, authorizing Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the state, to remove debris from the Fourmile Fire from public and private property. I understand that after September 30, 2011, Boulder County will begin mandatory debris removal procedures on private properties that have not complied with previous debris removal requests and offers of assistance. Thus, I am extending the debris authorization removal authority again. By statute, however, in order to authorize debris removal I must also declare a disaster emergency, the duration of which is limited to thirty days from the date of the executive order making the declaration. A portion of those funds are being used by Boulder County to fund a Boulder Fourmile Recovery Manager position. The County has determined that the position will be necessary and should continue through September 2012. In order to permit the County to effectively manage the recovery, I am extending the availability of the funds made available by Executive Order D 2010-013 through September 20, 2012. I continue to authorize Boulder County, as an instrumentality of the State, to remove and properly dispose of debris or wreckage from the Fourmile Fire from public or private property in Boulder County, Colorado. I acknowledge and find that on October 7, 2010, Boulder County presented ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2011-024 July 27, 2011 Page 3 of 3 to me an unconditional authorization for the removal of such debris or wreckage from public or private property and, in the case of removal of debris or wreckage from private property, has agreed to indemnify the state government against any claim arising from such removal. Hickenlooper Governor D 2012-028 EXECUTIVE ORDER Creating StudyColorado within the Department of Higher Education Pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the authority vested in the Office of the Governor, I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order creating StudyColorado, a program within the Colorado Department of Higher Education. I. Background, Need, and Purpose International students contribute directly to Colorado's economy and support Colorado businesses. It is estimated, for the 2010-2011 academic year, that international students and their dependents contributed almost $165 million in tuition and fees to the Colorado economy, and a total of over $235 million when living expenses are factored in. Equally important to the economic impact to the state, international students enrich our campuses and teach our students to collaborate across cultures and borders. When they return to their home country, international students become "ambassadors" for Colorado, promoting our state with family, friends and-later, when they graduate and enter the workforce- business colleagues. In many cases, international students who have studied in Colorado have gone on to influential positions in their home countries. Colorado benefits from the relationships established by these students during their months or years at our institutions. Colorado's businesses also benefit from international students. The Governor's Trade and Tourism Ambassador Program (TTAP) was established by Executive Order D2011-004 on January 11, 2011 to help integrate Colorado into the global economy with the express purpose of promoting the export of Colorado goods and services to other countries, persuading foreign investors to establish or expand operations in Colorado, and attracting more tourists to the state's year-round attractions. TTAP Ambassadors in turn established increasing the number of ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2012-028 July 6, 2012 Page 2 of 4 international students in Colorado as a top priority due to the broad potential impact across all three areas of exports, foreign investment and tourism. Many of our institutions of higher education are seeking to diversify their student bodies and many are actively recruiting international students. As a state, however, Colorado remains well below average in the number of international students. Similarly, when ranked by the overall size of the population, Colorado falls short in the number of international students it attracts. Colorado can add to the efforts of the institutions with a statewide marketing effort that promotes Colorado as a study destination and leverages the state's trade and tourism activities. Il. Mission and Scope The mission of StudyColorado will be to attract international students to Colorado through the unified outreach efforts of the state, higher education, and the business community. StudyColorado, with its partners, will engage students to form lifelong connections with Colorado. A. StudyColorado's goals will be to: i. ii. ili. iv. Support the international enrollment goals of the state's institutions of higher education; Create new economic opportunities for Colorado businesses through the influx of international students and their families; Create a more diverse learning environment to help Colorado students be more competitive in a global workplace; and Foster lasting relationships between international students and Colorado that will benefit international trade and investment. B. Study Colorado will achieve these goals by, among other activities: i. Developing a unique state-wide higher education brand and integrating it into key messaging for state leaders to promote Colorado higher education internationally; ii. Providing a forum for exchange of information related to international education; ili. Helping to create a welcoming culture for international students and visitors. In carrying out its activities, StudyColorado will engage with non-profit and other organizations in Colorado related to target countries including, but not limited to, foreign consulates and ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2012-028 July 6, 2012 Page 3 of 4 country-focused organizations such as the Canada-Colorado Association, US-Mexico Foundation, and Japan America Society of Colorado. IlI. Membership and Board of Directors A. Membership in StudyColorado will include institutions of higher education that i. Are accredited by the Higher Learning Commission of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools; ii. Are headquartered in the State of Colorado; and ili. Support the mission and goals of StudyColorado. Each member institution shall designate an individual as a representative to StudyColorado. StudyColorado may have as members other organizations as agreed by its Board of Directors. B. StudyColorado will have a Board of Directors, the membership of which will include but not be limited to: i. The Executive Director of the Department of Higher Education or his/her designee; ii. The Executive Director of the Office of Economic Development and International Trade or his/her designee; ili. At least five representatives of higher education institutions selected by a vote of all higher education member institutions, each for a term of three years; iv. At least four representatives from the Colorado business community, who may include members of the Governor's Trade and Tourism Ambassador Program, appointed by the Governor, each for a term of three years. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2012-028 July 6, 2012 Page 4 of 4 IV. Staffing and Resources StudyColorado will be housed within the Colorado Department of Higher Education, which shall provide necessary administrative support. StudyColorado shall have the power to accept gifts, grants and donations and to collect fees, consistent with Colorado law, from institutions of higher education, private entities and persons for purposes consistent with its mission and goals. Any money contributed to StudyColorado shall be directed to the Department of Higher Education. V. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in force until further modification or rescission by the Governor. Slash and burn pile operations in this area will reduce the risk of devastating wildfires, in addition to helping firefighters control such outbreak when they do occur. These fuel treatment activities not only reduce wildfire potential, but work to increase the heath of forests, by thinning forest strands and eliminating weak and diseased trees. Weaker trees that remain in the forest are prone to insect attacks and disease. In order to best serve the residents on the wildland-urban interface and promote the health and wellbeing of our forests, slash pile burning remains the least expensive and most effective ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2013-002 January 30, 2012 Page 2 of 3 method of removing slash. This procedure is conducted with caution and consideration, as projects are planed months and sometimes years in advance. This Division of Fire Prevention and Control will work to ensure continued safety and protection for residents on the wildland- urban interface, while promoting the health and longevity of our State's natural forests through properly regulated pile burnings. Executive Order D 2012-006 (State-wide suspension on prescribed or controlled fires) is hereby amended to allow for the resumption of slash pile burnings under controlled conditions. B. C. The Division of Fire Prevention and Control shall observe the following minimum guidelines for prescribed pile fires: 1. Ignition of piles shall occur only on days when there is adequate snow cover and the Colorado Air Pollution Control Division has determined that weather conditions are appropriate for burning because good smoke dispersal can be achieved; 2. Piles shall be ignited as early in the morning as possible and operations will cease before sunset; 3. Fire suppression resources shall be on site when piles are burned; and 4. Hickenlooper overnor D 2014-003 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a State of Disaster Emergency Due to Extreme Winter Weather and Authorizing a Temporary Exception to the Hours-of-Service Regulations for Commercial Motor Vehicles Used in the Transportation of Propane Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-700, et seq., and specifically C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(7)(a), I, John W. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to extreme weather conditions and suspending the hours-of-service regulations in Colorado Revised Statutes § 42-4-235, to the extent that the requirements therein prevent drivers of commercial motor vehicles who are working on this emergency from transporting propane winter heating fuel. Background and Purpose Temperatures in Colorado have dropped below zero for consecutive weeks. The recent extreme winter weather has caused an emergency situation by significantly reducing the availability of propane and impeding the delivery of necessary propane to many areas of Colorado. The extreme winter weather caused the cost of propane to skyrocket across the country and significantly reduced the supply. The commercial vehicle industry is impeded from continuing statewide propane fuel delivery operations for winter heating purposes. As a result, many Coloradans are left without a mechanism to heat their homes. The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin." C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). Colorado Revised Statutes § 42-4-235, adopting hours-of-service regulations from 49 C.F.R. 395, sets the hours which commercial vehicle drivers may operate. Those restrictions are impeding the commercial vehicle industry from delivering fuel to Coloradans in need. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2014-003 February 7, 2014 Page 2 of 2 Il. Declaration and Directives I declare and direct, as follows: A. The provisions of C.R.S. § 42-4-235 are hereby suspended to the extent that they prevent the delivery of necessary propane winter heating fuel to distribution points within Colorado. B. The above mentioned directive is subject to the following conditions: i. This exception shall not be construed as an exemption from C.R.S. Title 42, Traffic Code, as it relates to general motor vehicle safety, state and federal financial responsibility requirements, commercial driver's license requirements, size and weight regulations, or any federal motor carrier safety regulations not specifically identified herein. ii. This exception shall also not be construed as an exemption from 49 CFR 392.4 which prohibits ill or fatigued drives from operating a motor vehicle. ili. Motor carriers or drivers currently subject to an out-of-state service order issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration are not eligible for the exception until that order expires or the conditions have been met. Ill. Duration Unless amended or terminated by subsequent executive order, this order shall remain in effect through March 7, 2014. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this seventh day of February, 2014 The Haulaper John W. Hickenlooper Governor *r. 5 1 5 ---PAGE---

Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order implementing the 2014 Wildfire Preparedness Plan and designating moneys in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund for wildfire preparedness activities. 1. Background and Purpose The Director ("Director") of the Division of Fire Prevention and Control ("Division") is required to develop an annual Wildfire Preparedness Plan in collaboration with the County Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State Fire Chiefs' Association, the Director of the Office of Emergency Management, and the Adjutant General. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1227(2)(a). The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall be designed to address the following: (1) The amount of aerial firefighting resources necessary for the State of Colorado at times of high and low wildfire risk; (2) The availability of appropriate aerial firefighting equipment and personnel at times of high fire risk to respond to a wildfire; (3) The availability of state wildfire engines and staffing of the engines at different levels of wildfire risk; (4) The availability of wildfire hand crews, including state inmate wildfire hand crews, at different levels of wildfire risk; and (5) A process for ordering and dispatching aerial firefighting equipment and personnel that is consistent with, and supportive of, the statewide all-hazards resource mobilization plan prepared pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2014-008 May 12, 2014 Page 2 of 3 The Wildfire Preparedness Plan shall also provide recommendations on the use of the Wildfire Preparedness Fund created in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1227(1)(a). However, the draft could not be finalized because of uncertainty about the fire aviation program. The Director submitted a finalized plan to the Advisory Committee ("Advisory Committee") on Wildland Fire and Prescribed Fire Matters at its next regularly scheduled meeting on April 24, 2014. The Advisory Committee adopted the plan, and the Director submitted it to the Governor and Members of the General Assembly on April 28, 2014. The Wildfire Preparedness Plan reflects the collaboration of the County Sheriffs of Colorado, the Colorado State Fire Chiefs' Association, the Director of the Office of Emergency Management, and the Adjutant General. Il. Declaration and Directives A. The Division is hereby directed to implement the Wildfire Preparedness Plan for 2014 and carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified therein. B. The Division shall use the moneys in the Wildfire Preparedness Fund to implement and carry out the wildfire preparedness activities identified in the 2014 Wildfire Preparedness Plan, as is necessary. III. Hickenlooper, hereby issue this Executive Order employing the National Guard and authorizing the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety to encumber funds from the Resource Mobilization Fund for the purpose of assisting with the response to the Spruce Fire in Rocky Mountain National Park, Colorado. 1. Background and Purpose On Monday, June 30, 2014, a small fire was reported in Rocky Mountain National Park between Fern and Spruce Lakes. This fire, named the Spruce Fire, is in rugged terrain accessible only by air or by foot. By nightfall the fire grew to approximately one acre in size. The National Park Service assigned an Incident Management Team to manage the Spruce Fire. At approximately 1100 hours on July 1, 2014, the Incident Management Team requested a Colorado National Guard helicopter to be on standby for the emergency removal of people for medical purposes. The State of Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management received a valid resource order from the Pueblo Interagency Dispatch Center with appropriate financial codes committing the National Park Service to pay the State of Colorado for the cost of the helicopter mission as part of a shared resource with the Bureau of Land Management for the Eight Mile Fire. State personnel and the fire managers agreed to make the helicopter available as a shared resource at Buckley Air Force Base. I verbally approved the Division's request for a National Guard Helicopter at approximately 1300 hours on July 1, 2014. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2014-014 July 9, 2014 Page 2 of 2 Declaration and Directives A. B. Ill. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(6), I hereby authorize the Executive Director of the Department of Public Safety to encumber $5,000 from the Resource Mobilization Fund to pay for the use of the National Guard helicopter. Ultimately, the National Park Service will reimburse the Resource Mobilization Fund for their share of the actual costs expended for the National Guard helicopter and personnel. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. 9 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Emergency Management Director is hereby authorized and directed to allocate these funds to the appropriate government agencies and to execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of these funds. Hickenlooper, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order rescinding Executive Order D 2012-006. Background and Purpose On March 28, 2012, pursuant to Colorado Constitution, article IV, section 13 and C.R.S. 23-31- 308, we issued Executive Order D 2012-006 suspending prescribed or controlled fire on State or private lands pending review of agency protocols for prescribed or controlled fire. The suspension applied to all State lands as well as State agencies that applied prescribed or controlled fire on non-State lands under contracts or agreements with other entities. At the time, Colorado was experiencing unseasonably high temperatures and dry conditions which led to a number of wildfires across the State, and one fire, the Lower North Fork Fire, had been started by a prescribed or controlled burn. On April 13, 2012, the Lower North Fork Prescribed Fire Review (Bass Report) was issued, which made six recommendations for improving agency protocols around the use of prescribed burns. On January 30, 2013, pursuant to Colorado Constitution, article IV, section 13 and C.R.S. 23-31- 308, we issued Executive Order D 2013-002, which amended Executive Order D 2012-006, to allow for the resumption of slash pile burnings under controlled conditions in order to best protect residents on the wildland-urban interface and promote the health and well being of our forests. Broadcast burning however, remained banned pursuant to Executive Order D 2012- 006, pending a review of agency protocols. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2015-002 March 30, 2015 Page 2 of 3 On December 10, 2014, the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control (Division) issued its response to the Bass report recommendations. The response details the Division's evaluation, assessment and implementation of procedures in response to each of the Bass Report recommendations. Wildfires threaten public health and safety and can cause catastrophic damage to public and private resources, including clean air, clean water, fish and wildlife habitat, timber resources, forest soils, scenic beauty, recreational opportunities, economic and employment opportunities, and structures and other improvements. Prescribed burning, which reduces naturally occurring vegetative fuels within a variety of ecosystems, including forests and grasslands, reduces the risk and severity of major wildfire, thereby lessening the threat of fire and the resulting loss of life and property in those areas, including: A. When applied to forest lands, prescribed burning serves to reduce hazardous accumulations of fuels, prepare sites for both natural and artificial forest regeneration, improve wildlife habitat, control insects and disease, and perpetuate fire-dependent ecosystems; and B. When prescribed burning is used to manage fuels in wildland-urban interface areas, it substantially reduces the threat of damaging wildfire in urban communities. The Division has developed new guidelines and procedures for prescribed burning to ensure that all such burns are conducted in a safe and effective manner. These guidelines and procedures represent best practices for prescribed burning and have been subjected to peer evaluation and public comment. II. Declaration and Directives A. Executive Order D 2012-006 (Suspending Prescribed or Controlled Fire Pending Review of Protocols) is hereby rescinded to allow for the resumption of prescribed burning on State lands or by State agencies under controlled conditions. B. Prescribed fire operations conducted by State agencies or on State lands shall comply with the requirements of the Colorado Prescribed Burning Act (Senate Bill 13-083, as codified in C.R.S. Section 24-33.5-1201, et seq.) and the rules and guidelines promulgated by the Division, to ensure that all such burns are conducted in a safe and effective manner. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2015-002 March 30, 2015 Page 3 of 3 C. State agencies conducting prescribed burns shall observe the following additional guidelines for prescribed burning: 1. Prescribed burning shall occur only after a determination has been made that the property owner or other person having legal control of the property has both evaluated all alternatives to prescribed burning and concluded that prescribed burning is an appropriate hazardous fuel reduction method for the property; and 2. Prescribed burning shall occur only after proper notification of residents of potentially affected areas, local government officials, and the Division. D. The Division will work to ensure continued safety and protection for residents on the wildland-urban interface, while promoting the health and longevity of our State's natural forests through properly regulated prescribed burning. III. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect until rescinded or modified by Executive Order. Damage to public infrastructure began on April 28, 2015, and homes were lost to tornadoes on June 4, 2015. Record amounts of rainfall fell across Colorado, with widespread impacts being felt across many counties and municipalities. Some areas of the Eastern Plains experienced between 200% and 600% above average rainfall. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2015-005 July 2, 2015 Page 2 of 4 In many locations, excessive rainfall exceeded both daily and monthly precipitation records. Additional municipalities and counties-beyond those that have already declared an emergencies- continue to assess their damages and costs. Due to the excessive precipation, slope failures and slope instabilities may occur in the coming weeks even after the rains have subsided. Related to the weather conditions landslides have occurred across the state, particularly in Northwest Colorado. For example, both the northbound and southbound lanes of State Highway 13 ('SH 13") have experienced major damage. The severe weather resulting in the occurrence of persistent flooding, tornadoes, sinkholes, subsidence, erosion, landslides, debris flows, and associated agricultural impacts and infrastructure damage constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et. seq. The Governor's verbal order of May 9, 2015, declaring a dister emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. This order applies to the impacted communities east of the Continental Divide bounded by the north and south state borders and the Counties of Rio Blanco and Garfield in the Northwest part of the state. D. F. The Governor's verbal orders of May 9, 2015, pre-authorizing state assets for search and rescue efforts and verbal orders of May 24, 2015, authorizing the utilization of National Guard assets for any flood related missions, which include aerial damage assessment, are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this Executive Order. Emergency personnel anticipated that the rapid accumulation of snow and high winds had the potential to strand motorists throughout the area, thereby necessitating rescue missions. It was likely that the demand for rescue missions would exceed the capacity of local agencies. Accordingly, pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, Governor Hickenlooper verbally authorized the activation of the National Guard to assist these rescue missions. As the day progressed, the blizzard intensified, resulting in closures of numerous highways along the Front Range from the Wyoming border to Colorado Springs and throughout Northeastern Colorado. Denver International Airport shut down at approximately 12:17 p.m. as blizzard conditions triggered power fluctuations and required intensive snow removal. At approximately 3:40 p.m. on March 23, 2016, Governor Hickenlooper verbally declared a disaster emergency. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2016-002 March 25, 2016 Page 2 of 3 Il. Declaration and Directives A. The blizzard constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704. The Governor's verbal order of March 23, 2016 at 3:40 p.m. declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management, including the provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. Further, pursuant to the Colorado Constitution, Article IV, Section 5, and pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I also hereby authorize Colorado National Guard air resources to respond to impacts and events relating to the 2017 Solar Eclipse in northern Colorado. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the state and people presented by disasters. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as "the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin ...." C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). On Monday, August 21, 2017, a solar eclipse occurred with the path of totality crossing the nation from west to east, including portions of Wyoming and Nebraska. The event attracted interest across the nation, with an estimated 200 million people living within a one-day drive of the path of totality. A substantial number of people from Colorado made the journey to neighboring states, leading to traffic congestion, vehicle crashes, additional need for law enforcement and emergency medical services personnel and other associated impacts. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2017-020 September 11, 2017 Page 2 of 3 In the week prior to the 2017 Solar Eclipse, the Colorado Department of Transportation as well as other experts in the transportation arena predicted that the eclipse traffic could be the most significant traffic event of the year. There was significant concern that this would be a major traffic event - both from the heavy traffic volume as well as disruptions due to the eclipse. Experts predicted that up to 600,000 additional people would travel to Wyoming to view the eclipse. The Department of Transportation predicted that up to 400,000 additional people could be on Colorado roadways over the weekend and Monday August 21st. On August 18, 2017, the Colorado Department of Transportation warned drivers to be ready for an 8-12 hour wait to return home after the eclipse. In addition, the State Emergency Operations Center expected the traffic to overwhelm the response capabilities of local governments and private sector entities. Due to the information and projections of significant traffic and delays leaving motorists on our highways for 8-12 hours and in anticipation of the potential impacts resulting from this, on August 18, 2017, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for responding to impacts related to the 2017 Solar Eclipse, and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery Plan, also known as the State Emergency Operations Plan. The State Emergency Operations Center began final preparations August 18, 2017 to support local and state agency emergency needs, and activated them August 20-21, 2017 to closely monitor conditions and provide for rapid response to local and state agency assistance requests. Of particular concern were anticipated requests for emergency medical evacuation of sick and injured patients that would require helicopter evacuation due to congested roadways in remote areas. Further, I authorized pre-positioning of Colorado National Guard air resources for impacts and events related to the 2017 Solar Eclipse in northern Colorado, including helicopter medical emergency transportation and wildland fire suppression. Colorado National Guard air resources were placed on standby beginning August 21, 2017, at 10:00 a.m. and continued until 5:00 p.m., and the State Emergency Operations Center provided staff to allow state agencies to organize responsive activities. The State provided direct assistance to local law enforcement through the Colorado State Patrol, the State Emergency Operations Center, and the Department of Transportation. The National Guard remained on standby, but their assistance was not ultimately necessary. II. Declarations and Directives A. The 2017 Solar Eclipse and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of August 18, 2017 declaring a disaster emergency to prepare for and respond to impacts of the 2017 Solar Eclipse is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this order. ---PAGE--- Executive Order D 2017-020 September 11, 2017 Page 3 of 3 B. C. I further encumber $30,000 in the Disaster Emergency Fund to pay for responding to the impacts related to the 2017 Solar Eclipse, including preparations and activating the State Emergency Operations Center since August 18, 2017, and placing Colorado National Guard personnel on standby August 21, 2017. D. My verbal orders of August 18, 2017, activating the Colorado National Guard and authorizing the use of Colorado National Guard aviation assets for 2017 Solar Eclipse missions are hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if they were contained within this order. II. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty days from August 18, 2017, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in paragraph IIc) above shall remain available for the described purposes for sixty (60) months from the date of this Executive Order. full_text: D 2020 032 EXECUTIVE ORDER Amending and Extending Executive Order D 2020 003 Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Presence of Coronavirus Disease 2019 in Colorado Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701 et seq. (Act), I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order amending and extending Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended by Executive Order D 2020 018, declaring a continued state of disaster emergency due to the presence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID- 19) in Colorado, and authorizing continued response activities associated with the disaster emergency to enable State agencies to coordinate response, recovery, and mitigation efforts. Further, pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I hereby authorize the continued employment of the Colorado National Guard to support and provide planning resources to State and local authorities as they respond to the presence of COVID-19 in the State. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to . . . epidemic.” C.R.S. § 24- 33.5-703(3). The threat currently posed by COVID-19, a respiratory illness that can spread from person to person, constitutes a disaster for purposes of the Act. On March 5, 2020, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment’s (CDPHE) public health laboratory confirmed the first presumptive positive COVID-19 test result in Colorado. Since then, the number of confirmed cases has continued to climb, and we have evidence of community spread throughout the State. I verbally declared a disaster emergency on March 10, 2020, and issued the corresponding Executive Order D 2020 003 on March 11, 2020. On March 25, 2020, I requested that the President of the United States declare a Major Disaster for the State of Colorado, pursuant to the Stafford Act and the President approved that request on March 28, 2020. The virus that causes COVID-19 is spread primarily by close contact between people and through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes. Public health experts Executive Order D 2020 032 April 8, 2020 Page 2 of 4 recommend we practice “social distancing,” or maintaining a physical distance of six (6) feet or more from other people, as a way to slow the spread of COVID-19. My administration, along with other State, local, and federal authorities, has taken a wide array of actions to mitigate the effects of the pandemic, prevent further spread, and protect against overwhelming our health care resources. COVID-19 also physically contributes to property loss, contamination, and damage due to its propensity to attach to surfaces for prolonged periods of time. The measures ordered through this Executive Order are designed to limit the spread and mitigate the harm caused by COVID-19 and protect our most vulnerable populations. This Executive Order amends and extends Executive Order D 2020 003 for an additional thirty (30) days, provides for additional resources, temporarily waives procurement statutes for purchases involving response activities related to COVID-19, and authorizes the implementation of a Crisis Standards of Care plan (CSC Plan). II. Amendments Section II of Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended by Executive Order D 2020 018, is amended as follows: 1. Section II.C. is amended to read as follows: Pursuant to C.R.S. §24-33.5-706(4)(b), the funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are insufficient; therefore, it is ordered that $23 million dollars ($23,000,000) be transferred from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund to the Disaster Emergency Fund. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4), I order that $68 million dollars ($68,000,000) from the Disaster Emergency Fund be encumbered for response activities related to the COVID-19. 2. Add the following new Section II.F.: F. I order that the Department of Personnel and Administration in cooperation with the Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management enter into leases and contracts to provide and prepare facilities that are suitable for overflow patients. 3. Add the following new Section II.G.: G. I authorize the temporary suspension of the following statutory requirements related to the State’s procurement of goods and services that are reasonably necessary to save lives, mitigate the effects of the pandemic, prevent further spread of COVID-19, and protect against overwhelming our health care system: C.R.S. § 7-90-801(1) (concerning the requirement that foreign entities file a statement of foreign entity authority, and concerning any filing penalties associated therewith, with the Secretary of State to contract with the State, but Executive Order D 2020 032 April 8, 2020 Page 3 of 4 maintaining the other statutory requirements concerning a foreign entity’s ability to transact business or conduct activities); C.R.S. § 24-17-204 (concerning contract submissions and corresponding analyses submitted to the Office of State Planning and Budget); C.R.S. § 24-30-1104(1)(h) (concerning the Department of Personnel’s performance of certain centralized functions and approval processes for the executive branch); C.R.S. § 24-50-503(1)(a)-(c), (f) (concerning certain threshold requirements for contracts for personal services, but maintaining the requirements for non-discrimination provisions and termination by the state for breach); C.R.S. § 24-102-206 (concerning disclosure, notice, and penalty requirements for contractors and subcontractors performing work outside of the United States or Colorado); C.R.S. § 24-106-103(3)(d) (concerning the time frame in which personal services contracts are to be added to the centralized contract management system); and C.R.S. § 24- 106-104 (concerning the types of contracts that may be used to best meet the interests of the state); and C.R.S. §§ 24-37.5-105(3)(g)-(k), (4), (4.5) (concerning the responsibilities and procedures for the acquisition of information technology). 4. Add the following new Section II.H.: H. On April 5, 2020, the Governor’s Expert Emergency Epidemic Response Committee (GEERC) met and recommended that I authorize the implementation of a CSC Plan. I verbally adopted the CSC Plan and authorized its activation by CDPHE’s Chief Medical Officer on April 5, 2020, as memorialized by this Executive Order. Nothing in the CSC Plan supplants State or federal anti-discrimination laws, and demographic information such as race, age, disability status, citizenship, immigration status, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or gender identity cannot be considered in triage or resource allocation decisions except as is medically relevant to the survivability of COVID-19. Executive Order D 2020 032 April 8, 2020 Page 4 of 4 III. Duration Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended by Executive Order D 2020 018 and as amended and extended by this Executive Order, shall expire thirty (30) days from April 8, 2020, unless modified, rescinded, or extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.C. of Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended, shall remain available for the described purposes for twelve (12) months from the date of this Executive Order. full_text: D 2020 044 EXECUTIVE ORDER Safer at Home Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order continuing stay at home requirements for vulnerable individuals and permitting the limited reopening of postsecondary institutions and certain business operations due to the presence of coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) in Colorado. I. Background and Purpose On March 5, 2020, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment’s (CDPHE) public health laboratory confirmed the first presumptive positive COVID-19 test result in Colorado. Since then, the number of confirmed cases has continued to climb, and there is community spread throughout the State. I verbally declared a disaster emergency on March 10, 2020, and on March 11, 2020, I issued the corresponding Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended by Executive Orders D 2020 018 and D 2020 032. On March 25, 2020, I requested that the President of the United States declare a Major Disaster for the State of Colorado, pursuant to the Stafford Act. The President approved that request on March 28, 2020. My administration, along with other State, local, and federal authorities, has taken a wide array of actions to mitigate the effects of the pandemic, prevent further spread, and protect against overwhelming our health care resources. The virus that causes COVID-19 is spread primarily by close contact between people and through respiratory droplets when an infected person coughs or sneezes. It can also be spread through contact with contaminated surfaces. Public health experts recommend we practice social distancing, or maintaining a physical distance of six (6) feet or more from other people, as a way to slow the spread of COVID-19. Evidence shows that social distancing and the Stay at Home Executive Order D 2020 017, as amended, have helped to slow the increase of cases and rate of infection. While we have seen indications that our efforts to “flatten the curve” are working, transmission of the virus continues to threaten Coloradans’ way of life and livelihoods. As we take steps to return Coloradans to work, we must continue to practice social distancing at a high level and implement other measures, such as limiting our social interactions, taking extra precautions for Vulnerable Individuals and wearing non-medical masks while in public, to Executive Order D 2020 044 April 26, 2020 Page 2 of 6 facilitate a step towards reopening the economy while protecting public health. While this is a first step toward resuming our daily lives, the State is monitoring the spread of COVID-19 and additional precautions may be necessary in the future. This Executive Order implements a number of measures that will allow many Coloradans to return to work while we maintain a sustainable level of social distancing. In particular, this Executive Order continues Social Distancing Requirements for all Coloradans and stay at home requirements for Vulnerable Individuals, permits the limited reopening of postsecondary institutions and certain business operations, and orders the Executive Director of CDPHE to amend or issue public health orders (PHO) consistent with the directives in this Executive Order. II. Directives A. Pursuant to Executive Order D 2020 041, normal in-person instruction at all P-12 schools in Colorado will be suspended until the scheduled end of the 2019-2020 regular school year. P-12 schools and school districts may use school buildings for providing services to students, educators, and families, including but not limited to: in-person small group instruction; staff professional development; food service; access to internet, devices, or instructional materials; special education services; or mental health supports. P-12 schools and school districts intending to provide these services must work in coordination with their local public health agency and must observe Social Distancing Requirements pursuant to applicable public health orders. B. I direct the Executive Director of the Colorado Department of Higher Education (CDHE) to work with CDPHE to identify those programs and courses at postsecondary institutions that cannot be taught remotely and require limited in- person instruction. C. All Vulnerable Individuals should Stay at Home, except when necessary to provide, support, perform, or operate Necessary Activities, Minimum Basic Operations, Critical Government Functions, Necessary Travel, or Critical Businesses, provided that Vulnerable Individuals cannot be compelled to perform in-person work for any business or government function, including a Critical Business or Critical Government Function. D. For purposes of this Executive Order, Vulnerable Individuals means: 1. Individuals who are 65 years and older; 2. Individuals with chronic lung disease or moderate to severe asthma; 3. Individuals who have serious heart conditions; 4. Individuals who are immunocompromised; Executive Order D 2020 044 April 26, 2020 Page 3 of 6 5. Pregnant women; and 6. Individuals determined to be high risk by a licensed healthcare provider. E. I direct all individuals who are sick or who test positive for COVID-19 to Stay at Home except as necessary to care for themselves or seek medical care. F. I direct employers to accommodate workers with childcare responsibilities and workers who live in the same household as a Vulnerable Person to the greatest extent possible by promoting telecommuting or other remote work options, flexible schedules, or other means. G. I direct the Colorado Civil Rights Division within the Department of Regulatory Agencies and CDPHE to provide guidance to prevent discrimination in the workplace related to COVID-19. Employers must provide reasonable accommodation and are prohibited from discriminating against employees who are showing symptoms of COVID-19 or who have been in contact with a known positive case of COVID-19. H. I direct the Executive Director of CDPHE to issue a new or amended PHO consistent with the directives in this Executive Order. The new or amended PHO must: 1. Advise Coloradans to wear non-medical cloth face coverings that cover the nose and mouth whenever in public; 2. Order Coloradans to limit: i. Social interactions to the greatest extent possible except as required to conduct Necessary Activities; and ii. Essential Travel to within their county of residence or employment as much as possible and recreational travel to no further than ten (10) miles from their residence. 3. Prohibit public gatherings of ten (10) persons or more in both public spaces and private commercial venues. 4. Strongly encourage all Critical Businesses, Critical Government Functions, Non-Critical Retail, and Non-Critical Commercial Businesses to allow workers to telecommute whenever possible. 5. Require all Critical Businesses, Critical Government Functions, Non-Critical Retail, and Non-Critical Commercial Businesses to make work accommodations for Vulnerable Individuals, who remain subject to Stay at Home requirements. Employers must also be encouraged to make Executive Order D 2020 044 April 26, 2020 Page 4 of 6 accommodations for individuals living in the same household as a Vulnerable Individual, and for individuals with childcare responsibilities. 6. Permit all Critical Businesses and Critical Government Functions to continue to operate with mandatory Social Distancing Requirements and cleaning protocols. 7. Permit Non-Critical Retail to operate and offer goods through delivery service, window service, walk-up service, drive-through service, drive-up service, curbside delivery, and, beginning May 1, 2020, permit Non-Critical Retail to allow customers onto their premises in a manner allowing for strict compliance with mandatory Social Distancing Requirements similar to the requirements for Critical Retail. 8. Permit Places of Public Accommodation to continue to offer food and beverage using delivery service, window service, walk-up service, drive- through service, drive-up service, curbside delivery or any manner set forth in an existing Executive Order or PHO and in accordance with mandatory Social Distancing Requirements. 9. Issue appropriate guidelines for classes and programs identified in consultation with the Executive Director of CDHE pursuant to paragraph II.B., above. 10. Beginning on May 4, 2020, permit Non-Critical Commercial Businesses to allow up to fifty percent (50%) of their employees to conduct in-person work that takes place outside a private residence in accordance with Mandatory Social Distancing Requirements and protocols. 11. Ensure that Critical Businesses, Critical Government Functions, Non-Critical Commercial Businesses, and Non-Critical Retail with over fifty (50) employees in any one location follow protocols established by PHO, including but not limited to symptom screening and temperature check stations, closure of common areas, cleaning protocols, and Mandatory Social Distancing Requirements and protocols. I. Any new or amended PHO issued pursuant to this Executive Order must identify or develop: 1. Mandatory Social Distancing Requirements and protocols to be implemented by all employers, identifying any specific protocols for certain employers based on the nature of their work, including proper face and hand coverings to be used; Executive Order D 2020 044 April 26, 2020 Page 5 of 6 2. An amended definition of Vulnerable Individual consistent with this Executive Order; and 3. Operations requirements for Non-Critical Retail and Critical Retail. J. I direct the Executive Director of the Colorado Department of Labor and Employment (CDLE) to promulgate and issue temporary emergency rules to amend the Colorado Health Emergency Leave with Pay Rules found in 7 CCR 1103-10 to cover individuals returning to work under this Executive Order and to extend paid sick leave coverage to up to two-thirds pay for fourteen (14) days if a worker has tested positive for COVID-19, has COVID-like symptoms, or has been directed to quarantine or isolation due to COVID-19 concerns. K. I direct the Executive Director of CDLE to promulgate and issue temporary emergency rules pursuant to C.R.S. § 8-73-108(4)(c) and guidance to ensure that workers, and particularly workers who are Vulnerable Individuals, are not in danger of losing unemployment insurance eligibility for refusal to return to COVID-19-related demonstrable, unsafe working conditions. L. Terms in this Executive Order, including Stay at Home, Necessary Activities, Minimum Basic Operations, Critical Government Functions, Necessary Travel, Critical Businesses, Places of Public Accommodation, Critical Retail, Social Distancing Requirements, and Vulnerable Individuals have the meaning as defined in PHO 20-24 and PHO 20-22, as amended, or any PHO issued pursuant to this Executive Order. M. Any county wishing to apply for a local variance from part or all of this Executive Order must submit a written application to CDPHE certifying that the county has low case counts of COVID-19 cases or can document fourteen (14) consecutive days of decline in COVID-19 cases reported in the county. The application must include a written COVID-19 suppression plan approved by the appropriate local public health authority, all hospitals within the county (unless no hospitals are located in the county), and a majority of the county commissioners, or, in the case of the City and County of Denver, the mayor of Denver, or, in the case of the City and County of Broomfield, the city council. N. CDPHE shall review and approve a county-specific COVID-19 suppression plan that meets CDPHE’s public health standards. CDPHE shall not provide COVID- 19 preparedness grant funding to any county that implements measures that are less restrictive than the standards contained in this Executive Order if the county did not first obtain approval from CDPHE to adopt such less restrictive standards. O. Nothing in this Executive Order prevents a county or municipality from adopting more protective standards than those contained in this Executive Order as Executive Order D 2020 044 April 26, 2020 Page 6 of 6 necessary, including but not limited to stay at home orders, mask wearing requirements in public, or additional protective measures. If adopted, such measures shall take effect in the county or municipality without the need for further approval by the State. 1. Except as modified by this Executive Order, all Executive Orders issued due to COVID-19 that are currently in effect shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from April 27, 2020, unless extended further by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty sixth day of April, 2020 Jared Polis Governor

full_text: D 2020 072 EXECUTIVE ORDER Ordering the Transfer of Funds from the Disaster Emergency Fund to the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund to Fund Firefighting Operations and Encumbering Funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund for Additional Wildfire Aviation Resources Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order ordering the transfer of funds from the Disaster Emergency Fund to the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund to fund firefighting operations, and encumbering funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund for additional wildfire aviation resources. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire . . . .” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). On March 5, 2020, the Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment’s (CDPHE) public health laboratory confirmed the first presumptive positive coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) test result in Colorado. Since then, the number of confirmed cases has continued to climb, and there is community spread throughout the State. I verbally declared a disaster emergency on March 10, 2020, and on March 11, 2020, I issued the corresponding Executive Order D 2020 003, as amended by Executive Orders D 2020 018, D 2020 032, and D 2020 058. On March 25, 2020, I requested that the President of the United States declare a Major Disaster for the State of Colorado, pursuant to the Stafford Act. The President approved that request on March 28, 2020. COVID-19 has strained our first responders as they have mobilized to save lives. As identified in the State’s 2020 Wildfire Preparedness Plan, local fire departments have reduced availability to provide response and assistance outside of their home jurisdiction, and firefighting resources from other states and federal agencies have limited capacity. COVID-19 creates challenges to maintaining the health of firefighters in fire camps and command posts, and poses a high risk of exposure among fire management personnel. Executive Order D 2020 072 May 21, 2020 Page 2 of 3 Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1226(2), the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund assists local jurisdictions with aerial tanker or firefighting helicopter support, as well as the employment of wildfire hand crews for initial attack on wildfires. The current balance of the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund is one hundred fifty two thousand two hundred and fifty three dollars ($152,253). Based on projected operational needs, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control within the Department of Public Safety estimates the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund will need an additional seven hundred sixty three thousand dollars ($763,000). These funds will enable the State to respond to the current circumstances presented by COVID-19. Colorado will use the funds for early detection and rapid initial attack actions to reduce the probability and impacts from large, extended wildfires. The State also needs additional aviation resources, specifically a Large Air Tanker, to adequately respond to wildfires. The use of a Large Air Tanker will enhance the State’s ability to contain fires, preserve resources, and keep firefighters and citizens out of dangerous environments. This Executive Order directs the transfer of funds from the Disaster Emergency Fund to the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund so that the Wildfire Emergency Response Fund has sufficient funds to assist local jurisdictions. full_text: D 2020 073 EXECUTIVE ORDER Amending Executive Order D 2016 010 to Increase and Extend the Availability of Funds for the Junkins Fire in Custer and Pueblo Counties Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order amending Executive Order D 2016 010 to increase and extend the availability of funds for the Junkins Fire in Custer and Pueblo Counties (Junkins Fire). I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire . . . .” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). On October 17, 2016, a fire ignited in Custer County. The fire, named the Junkins Fire, grew rapidly, consuming 15,751 acres by the end of the day. As the fire grew in size, 270 homes were threatened or placed on pre-evacuation orders in Custer and Pueblo Counties. The extreme fire conditions put lives and property at risk. The fire exceeded Custer County’s fire suppression capabilities, and Custer County declared a local emergency on October 17, 2016. Also on October 17, 2016, the State’s Division of Fire Prevention and Control determined that the Junkins Fire was eligible for the Emergency Fire Fund. However, due to previous fires, the Emergency Fire Fund did not have funds available for the Junkins Fire. On the same day, Governor John Hickenlooper issued Executive Order D 2016 010 declaring a disaster emergency for the Junkins Fire, authorizing the use of the Colorado National Guard, transferring seven million dollars ($7,000,000) into the Disaster Emergency Fund from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund, and encumbering seven million dollars ($7,000,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund to pay for fire suppression, response, and recovery efforts related to the Junkins Fire. On October 18, 2016, the Federal Emergency Management Agency approved a federal Fire Management Assistance Grant to support fire suppression activities for the Junkins Fire. Executive Order D 2020 073 May 21, 2020 Page 2 of 2 The impacts of the Junkins Fire require additional funds for ongoing response, recovery, and mitigation efforts. Accordingly, this Executive Order amends Executive Order D 2016 010 to increase and extend the availability of funds for the Junkins Fire. II. Amendment Section II.C of Executive Order D 2016 010 is amended to read as follows: Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund are hereby found insufficient to pay for fire suppression efforts related to the Junkins Fire. I therefore transfer seven million dollars ($7,000,000) into the Disaster Emergency Fund from the Controlled Maintenance Trust Fund. I further encumber eight million five hundred thousand dollars ($8,500,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund to pay for the fire suppression, response, and recovery efforts related to the Junkins Fire since the inception of the fire. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), I hereby authorize and direct the Emergency Management Director to allocate these funds to the appropriate government agencies and to execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of these funds. These funds shall remain available for this purpose for forty- eight (48) months from October 17, 2016, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. III. Duration This Executive Order shall remain in effect unless modified or rescinded by Executive Order. In all other respects, Executive Order D 2016 010 shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty-first day of May, 2020 Jared Polis Governor

full_text: D 2020 106 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular. pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating up to six (6) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2020 state primary election. I. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support during the 2020 state primary election. By activating up to six (6) members of the National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election defense efforts up to and including the 2020 state primary election, which is on June 30, 2020. Executive Order D 2020 106 June 16, 2020 Page 2 of 2 II. Directives On June 8, 2020, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2020 state primary election. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, the Governor may employ the National Guard for the defense of the State. I hereby activate up to six (6) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2020 state primary election. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from June 16, 2020, unless extended further by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this sixteenth day of June, 2020. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: D 2020 124 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency and Authorizing Employment of the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Protecting Municipal and State Buildings in Denver Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to civil unrest in Denver. Further, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I hereby authorize employing up to one hundred (100) members of the Colorado National Guard to assist with protecting municipal and state buildings in Denver. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin . . . .” C.R.S. § 24-33.5- 703(3). In May 2020, the killing of George Floyd sparked demonstrations in Denver and across the country. While most of the protests and demonstrations were peaceful, there were some incidents of vandalism and violence in downtown Denver. Denver law enforcement agencies requested mutual aid from neighboring cities. Those cities supplied Denver with additional support. By May 30, 2020, the need to protect property owned by the City and County of Denver and the State of Colorado exceeded the capabilities of Denver law enforcement agencies and mutual aid provided by neighboring cities. Denver requested that the Governor authorize employment of up to one hundred (100) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to provide additional support to law enforcement to protect eight buildings owned by the City and County of Denver, and one building belonging to the State of Colorado. At approximately 10:45 AM on May 30, 2020, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to civil unrest in Denver and the need to provide additional support for protecting municipal and State buildings in Denver. I authorized activating up to one hundred (100) unarmed Executive Order D 2020 124 July 6, 2020 Page 2 of 3 members of the Colorado National Guard to provide the requested support and security in Denver. I also activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan. II. Declarations and Directives A. The civil unrest in Denver constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S § 24- 33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order on May 30, 2020, declaring a disaster emergency and authorizing employment and use of the Colorado National Guard is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3- 104, I have determined that it is in the best interest of the people of Colorado to employee up to one hundred (100) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to provide support and security for civil unrest in Denver. To ensure timely reimbursement to the Colorado National Guard, I authorize encumbering two hundred thousand dollars ($200,000) from the Disaster Emergency Fund, established in C.R.S § 24-33.5-706(2)(a), to pay the Colorado National Guard for costs associated with personnel. This amount is currently available in the Disaster Emergency Fund. Seventy-five percent (75%) of costs incurred by the Colorado National Guard for support and security for Denver City and County buildings are to be reimbursed by Denver to the State of Colorado. The remaining twenty-five percent (25%) of costs for support and security will be paid by the State of Colorado. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate funding to the Colorado National Guard and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. The funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for this purpose until six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. Executive Order D 2020 124 July 6, 2020 Page 3 of 3 III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from May 30, 2020, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for the described purposes for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this sixth day of July, 2020. Jared Polis Governor
