full_text: D 2022 022 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring and Extending a Disaster Emergency Due to Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring and extending a state of disaster emergency due to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado, enabling State agencies to coordinate for mitigation of disease spread, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) was initially detected in the United States in the wild bird population in January 2022 in South Carolina and in the domestic poultry population in February 2022 in Indiana. It continues to spread across the United States. The disease spreads rapidly among wild and domestic poultry. It has a mortality rate above ninety percent. HPAI was first detected in wild birds in Colorado on March 24, 2022. The disease was detected in domestic poultry on April 8, 2022. As of May 26, 2022, HPAI has been confirmed in 14 Colorado counties, with cases occurring in wild, domestic, and commercial flocks. On April 19, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial broiler breeder facility in Montrose County, affecting 58,000 birds. On April 29, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial table egg layer facility in Weld County, affecting 1.4 million birds and more than seven million eggs. Depopulation of both facilities is required. The United States Department of Agriculture has limited staff to support depopulation activities, and requires the support of State agencies, including the Colorado Department of Agriculture, Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, and the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management. Executive Order D 2022 022 May 28, 2022 Page 2 of 3 On April 29, 2022, at approximately 6:41 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. This Executive Order memorializes that verbal declaration and extends the declaration of a disaster emergency for an additional thirty days due to the ongoing need to identify HPAI cases and potential for further response to commercial poultry facilities. II. Declarations and Directives A. HPAI in Colorado and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of April 29, 2022, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, and the Food and Agriculture Incident Annex of the the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are hereby found insufficient to pay for disease mitigation, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the HPAI in Colorado. Therefore, I order that one million dollars ($1,000,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SER) to the DEF. I encumber one million dollars ($1,000,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund, established in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a), for costs associated with the State’s disease mitigation, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado since April 29, 2022. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. The funds described in Section II.C above shall remain available for this purpose until six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. Executive Order D 2022 022 May 28, 2022 Page 3 of 3 E. The Office of Emergency Management, in coordination with the Colorado Department of Agriculture, is authorized to coordinate application for any funds available related to this disaster emergency. Specifically, the Colorado Department of Agriculture is directed to seek reimbursement, including reimbursement from the United States Department of Agriculture for response activities under the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Emergency Cooperative Agreement, and make payments as needed to agencies providing assistance on this incident. III. Duration This Executive Order, declaring and extending the disaster emergency, shall expire thirty (30) days from May 28, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.C above shall remain available for the described purposes for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order. full_text: D 2022 026 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating up to six (6) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2022 State primary election. I. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support from June 13, 2022, through June 30 2022, for the 2022 State primary election. By activating up to six (6) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election defense efforts up to and including the 2022 State primary election on June 28, 2022. Executive Order D 2022 026 June 9, 2022 Page 2 of 2 II. Declarations and Directives On May 3, 2022, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2022 State primary election occurring on June 28, 2022. As of August 16, 2018, the Cabin Lake Fire burned approximately 5,727 acres on state and federal land with 29% containment. On August 16, 2018, at approximately 4:45 PM, the Division of Fire Prevention and Control determined that the Cabin Lake Fire qualified for funds from the Emergency Fire Fund. On August 16, 2018, at approximately 5:00 PM, Governor John Hickenlooper verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Cabin Lake Fire and activated the State of Colorado Hazard and Incident Response and Recovery Plan (“State Emergency Operations Plan”). On September 7, 2018, Lieutenant Governor Donna Lynne, acting on behalf of the State while Governor Hickenlooper was absent from the State, issued Executive Order D 2018 023, memorializing Governor Hickenlooper’s verbal order and allocating $350,000 to pay for fire suppression, recovery, and mitigation efforts related to the Cabin Lake Fire. full_text: D 2022 030 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Menkhaven Fire in Conejos County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Menkhaven Fire in Conejos County enabling State agencies to coordinate for fire suppression, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire.” C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). The Menkhaven Fire started on May 28, 2022, in Conejos County west of Antonito, Colorado. Due to dry conditions, the Menkhaven Fire quickly spread to 153 acres in inaccessible terrain, threatening 31 single residences. Critical fire weather and a large number of spot fires in front of the main fire created the potential for significant additional growth and evacuations. On May 28, 2022, at approximately 5:48 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Menkhaven Fire in Conejos County and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. As of June 7, 2022, the Menkhaven Fire burned 242 acres and was 100% contained. II. Declarations and Directives A. The Menkhaven Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of May 28, 2022, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. Executive Order D 2022 030 June 26, 2022 Page 2 of 3 B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5- 706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are hereby found insufficient to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the Menkhaven Fire. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. E. The Division of Fire Prevention and Control, via its fire billing practices, is authorized to coordinate application for any funds available related to this disaster emergency. Executive Order D 2022 030 June 26, 2022 Page 3 of 3 III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from May 28, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for the described purposes for thirty-six (36) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty-sixth day of June 2022. Jared Polis Governor

I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) was initially detected in the United States in the wild bird population in January 2022 in South Carolina and in the domestic poultry population in February 2022 in Indiana. It continues to spread across the United States. The disease spreads rapidly among wild and domestic poultry. It has a mortality rate above ninety percent. HPAI was first detected in wild birds in Colorado on March 24, 2022. The disease was detected in domestic poultry on April 8, 2022. As of May 26, 2022, HPAI has been confirmed in 14 Colorado counties, with cases occurring in wild, domestic, and commercial flocks. On April 19, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial broiler breeder facility in Montrose County, affecting 58,000 birds. On April 29, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial table egg layer facility in Weld County, affecting 1.4 million birds and more than seven million eggs. Depopulation of both facilities is complete. The United States Department of Agriculture had limited staff to support depopulation activities, and required the support of State agencies, including the Colorado Department of Agriculture, Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, and the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management. Executive Order D 2022 031 June 26, 2022 Page 2 of 2 While the overall HPAI case trends across the country continue to decline, the risk for disease introductions remains as additional detections are made in wild bird populations. Two additional commercial sites were identified in Weld County on June 7, 2022 and June 9, 2022, impacting 2.2 million chickens. Depopulation, disposal, and virus elimination activities continue at both sites. This Executive Order extends Executive Order D 2022 022 due to the ongoing need to identify HPAI cases and potential for further response to commercial poultry facilities for an additional thirty days. II. Duration Executive Order D 2022 022, as extended by this Executive Order, shall expire thirty (30) days from June 26, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.C shall remain available for the described purposes for six (6) months from the date of Executive Order D 2022 022. In all other respects, Executive Order D 2022 022 shall remain in full force and effect as originally promulgated. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty-sixth day of June 2022. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: D 2022 039 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado, enabling State agencies to coordinate for mitigation of disease spread, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) was initially detected in the United States in the wild bird population in January 2022 in South Carolina and in the domestic poultry population in February 2022 in Indiana. Following a short summer reprieve, it resumed spreading across the United States. The disease spreads rapidly among wild and domestic poultry. It has a mortality rate above ninety percent. HPAI was first detected in wild birds in Colorado on March 24, 2022. The disease was detected in domestic poultry on April 8, 2022. As of September 21, 2022, HPAI has been confirmed in 17 Colorado counties, with cases occurring in wild, domestic, and commercial flocks. On April 19, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial broiler breeder facility in Montrose County, affecting 58,000 birds. On April 29, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial table egg layer facility in Weld County, affecting 1.4 million birds and more than seven million eggs. Both facilities were depopulated. On April 29, 2022, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado which was memorialized in Executive Order 2022 022. Executive Order 2022 022 was extended in May and June 2022, and expired on July 25, 2022 as the mitigation, consequence management and recovery efforts caused a decline in the HPAI case trends. On September 20, 2022, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial facility in Weld County, affecting approximately 1.1 million birds. Depopulation of the facility is required. The United States Department of Agriculture has limited staff to support depopulation activities, and requires the support of State agencies, including the Colorado Department of Agriculture, Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment, and the Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management. On September 21, 2022, at approximately 9:45 AM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. This Executive order memorializes that verbal declaration. II. Declarations and Directives A. HPAI in Colorado and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of September 21, 2022, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, and the Food and Agriculture Incident Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. In Executive Order D 2022 022, I ordered that one million dollars ($1,000,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SER) to the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF). I encumbered one million dollars ($1,000,000) in the Disaster Emergency Fund, established in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a), for costs associated with the State’s disease mitigation, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado since April 29, 2022. A portion of the one million dollars ($1,000,000) I encumbered in Executive Order D 2022 022 remains available for the State’s efforts related to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza. Accordingly, the total amount of funds previously encumbered shall remain encumbered for costs associated with the State’s disease mitigation, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado throughout 2022. In Executive Order D 2022 022, I directed that the funds encumbered shall remain available for six (6) months from the date of that Executive Order, which was May 28, 2022. As described in Section II.D below, these funds shall now remain available for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. The funds described in Section II.C above shall remain available for this purpose until six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. E. The Office of Emergency Management, in coordination with the Colorado Department of Agriculture, is authorized to coordinate application for any funds available related to this disaster emergency. Specifically, the Colorado Department of Agriculture is directed to seek reimbursement, including reimbursement from the United States Department of Agriculture for response activities under the 2022 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Emergency Cooperative Agreement, and make payments as needed to agencies providing assistance on this incident. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from September 21, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.C above shall remain available for the described purposes for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty-ninth day of September 2022. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: D 2022 042 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2022 General Election. I. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support on October 31, 2022 and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2022 General Election. By activating up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election defense efforts up to and including the 2022 General Election on November 8, 2022. Executive Order D 2022 042 October 31, 2022 Page 2 of 2 II. Declarations and Directives On October 25, 2022, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2022 General Election occurring on November 8, 2022. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, the Governor may employ the National Guard for the defense of the State. I hereby activate up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to participate in training activities and assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts on October 31 2022, and extending for up to thirty days, for the 2022 General Election. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from October 31, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order. full_text: Executive Order D 2023 002 January 13, 2023 Page 1 of 3 D 2023 002 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to Extreme Cold Temperatures Throughout Colorado and Authorizing Deployment of the Colorado National Guard Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to extreme winter weather throughout the State of Colorado, enabling State agencies to coordinate response, recovery, and mitigation activities. Further, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I hereby authorize deploying the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of responding to extreme winter weather and providing support. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin…” C.R.S. § 24- 33.5-703(3). On December 20, 2022, the National Weather Service predicted an arctic blast that would impact Colorado, with a dangerous mix of sub-zero temperatures and strong wind and snow right before the beginning of the holiday travel season. With these dangerous conditions, children, the elderly, people with disabilities, people with special medical needs, and unhoused individuals are especially vulnerable. The Colorado National Guard is the most effective available resource to support extreme winter weather response, including assisting local communities to help keep people safe during dangerously cold temperatures. On December 20, 2022, at approximately 11:40 AM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the State of Colorado, activating the State Emergency Operations Plan and directing the Office of Emergency Management (OEM) to take all necessary and appropriate State actions to assist the affected jurisdictions with their response, recovery, and mitigation efforts. This declaration also authorized the use of funds and permits of the Special Delegation of the State Controller’s Contract Signature Authority, and allowed OEM to mobilize State resources and contracts and awards using Emergency Procurement Procedures, and encumbered and expended those funds as determined by the Director of OEM or his delegate. At the same Executive Order D 2023 002 January 13, 2023 Page 2 of 3 time, I verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for extreme winter weather response and support. II. Declarations and Directives A. The extreme winter weather and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of December 20, 2022, declaring a disaster emergency, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, my verbal order of December 20, 2022, authorizing deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for extreme winter weather response and support is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. C. My verbal order of December 20, 2022, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or his delegate of the OEM pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. D. To ensure timely reimbursement to the Colorado National Guard, I order that one hundred twenty thousand dollars ($120,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SER) to the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF), established in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a). I further order that one hundred twenty thousand dollars ($120,000) be encumbered from the DEF to pay the Colorado National Guard for costs associated with personnel. E. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the OEM is hereby authorized and directed to allocate funding to the Colorado National Guard and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of funds. The funds described in Section II(D) above shall remain available for this purpose for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. Executive Order D 2023 002 January 13, 2023 Page 3 of 3 III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from December 20, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(D) above shall remain available for the described purposes for six (6) months from the date of this Executive Order. full_text: D 2023 003 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Fuel Supply Chain Risk in Colorado Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the fuel supply chain risk in Colorado, enabling State agencies to coordinate for response and mitigation efforts. Further, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, I hereby authorize deploying the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of assisting with planning and logistics related to the fuel supply chain risk in Colorado. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin…” C.R.S. § 24- 33.5-703(3). Suncor’s Commerce City refinery processes approximately 98,000 barrels of oil per day, and contributes $2.5 billion to Colorado’s economy annually. Approximately 95% of Suncor’s products are sold within Colorado, accounting for roughly 25% of statewide gasoline consumption, 50% of statewide diesel consumption, and one third of jet fuel consumption at the Denver International Airport. Coinciding with extreme and record-setting cold weather impacting Colorado in December 2022, Suncor’s Commerce City refinery experienced equipment damage and has been shut down to enable inspection and repair of damaged equipment. Suncor estimates resuming production in six to twelve weeks. The shutdown will result in significant fuel supply challenges throughout Colorado. On December 31, 2022, at approximately 4:35 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the State of Colorado due to fuel supply chain risk, activating the State Emergency Operations Plan and directing the Office of Emergency Management (OEM) to take all necessary and appropriate State actions to assist the State with its response and mitigation efforts. Executive Order D 2023 003 January 27, 2023 Page 2 of 3 I further verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of assisting with planning and logistics related to the fuel supply chain risk in Colorado. I have contacted refineries and fuel transportation companies in other parts of the country to minimize any disruption and to maximize distribution of fuel to Coloradans. My fellow Governors in neighboring states are helping coordinate additional deliveries to Colorado. My administration is pursuing every avenue to mitigate the impacts of Suncor’s temporary shutdown, including temporarily suspending statute and making temporary regulatory exemptions to facilitate the expeditious delivery of fuel around the State. State agencies are proactively reviewing additional tools available to ensure that adequate fuel supply can reach distributors throughout the State. II. Declarations and Directives A. The shutdown of Suncor’s Commerce City refinery for six to twelve weeks poses a fuel supply chain risk in Colorado which constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of December 31, 2022, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, my verbal order of December 31, 2022, authorizing deployment and use of the National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of assisting with planning and logistics related to the fuel supply chain risk in Colorado is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. C. My verbal order of December 31, 2022, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or his delegate of the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. D. I direct the Colorado Department of Transportation to issue non-interstate overweight indivisible permits pursuant to C.R.S. § 42-4-510 to motor carriers involved in gasoline and fuel transportation to travel on state highways with heavier loads to increase the volume of fuel delivered and reduce the total number of trucks required to deliver that fuel. E. I direct the Colorado State Patrol (CSP) to temporarily suspend certain provisions of C.R.S. § 42-4-235, as outlined by CSP, to the extent that they prevent the delivery of necessary fuel to distribution points within Colorado, subject to the following conditions: Executive Order D 2023 003 January 27, 2023 Page 3 of 3 i. This Executive Order notwithstanding, all drivers, companies, and entities involved in the transportation and delivery of fuel shall prioritize safe practices in all phases of transportation and delivery of fuel. Further, this exception shall not be construed as an exemption from C.R.S. Title 42, Traffic Code, as it relates to general motor vehicle safety, state and federal financial responsibility requirements, commercial driver’s license requirements, size and weight regulations, or any federal motor carrier safety regulations not specifically identified herein. ii. This exception shall also not be construed as an exemption from 49 C.F.R. § 392.3 which prohibits ill or fatigued drivers from operating a motor vehicle. iii. Motor carriers or drivers currently subject to an out-of-service order issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration are not eligible for the exception until that order expires or the conditions of the order have been met. F. I urge the Attorney General’s Office to pursue any violations of the Colorado Consumer Protection Act, C.R.S. § 6-1-730 et seq., relating to the price of fuel, including charging excessive prices and engaging in price gouging. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from December 31, 2022, unless extended further by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this twenty-seventh day of January, 2023. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: Executive Order D 2023 004 January 30, 2023 Page 1 of 3 D 2023 004 EXECUTIVE ORDER Renewing a Disaster Emergency Due to the Ongoing Fuel Supply Chain Risk in Colorado Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order renewing a state of disaster emergency due to the ongoing fuel supply chain risk in Colorado, enabling State agencies to coordinate for response and mitigation efforts. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin…” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). Suncor’s Commerce City refinery processes approximately 98,000 barrels of oil per day, and contributes $2.5 billion to Colorado’s economy annually. Approximately 95% of Suncor’s products are sold within Colorado, accounting for roughly 25% of statewide gasoline consumption, 50% of statewide diesel consumption, and one third of jet fuel consumption at the Denver International Airport. Coinciding with extreme and record-setting cold weather impacting Colorado in December 2022, Suncor’s Commerce City refinery experienced equipment damage and has been shut down to enable inspection and repair of damaged equipment. Suncor estimates resuming production in four to six weeks. The shutdown will result in significant fuel supply challenges throughout Colorado, and has caused increased gas prices across the State. On December 31, 2022, at approximately 4:35 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the State of Colorado due to fuel supply chain risk, activating the State Emergency Operations Plan and directing the Office of Emergency Management (OEM) to take all necessary and appropriate State actions to assist the State with its response and mitigation efforts. I also verbally authorized deployment and use of the Colorado National Guard, though the National Guard was not ultimately needed. Executive Order D 2023 004 January 30, 2023 Page 2 of 3 On January 30, 2023, at approximately 2:15 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the State of Colorado due to the ongoing fuel supply chain risk in Colorado. My verbal declaration renewed the disaster emergency for another thirty days. I have contacted refineries and fuel transportation companies in other parts of the country to minimize any disruption and to maximize distribution of fuel to Coloradans. My fellow Governors in neighboring states are helping coordinate additional deliveries to Colorado. My administration is pursuing every avenue to mitigate the impacts of Suncor’s temporary shutdown, including temporarily suspending statute and making temporary regulatory exemptions to facilitate the expeditious delivery of fuel around the State. State agencies are proactively reviewing additional tools available to ensure that adequate fuel supply can reach distributors throughout the State. II. Declarations and Directives A. The shutdown of Suncor’s Commerce City refinery for an additional four to six weeks poses an ongoing fuel supply chain risk in Colorado which constitutes a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of January 30, 2023, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. My verbal order of January 30, 2023, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or his delegate of the Office of Emergency Management pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. I direct the Colorado Department of Transportation to issue non-interstate overweight indivisible permits pursuant to C.R.S. § 42-4-510 to motor carriers involved in gasoline and fuel transportation to travel on state highways with heavier loads to increase the volume of fuel delivered and reduce the total number of trucks required to deliver that fuel. D. I direct the Colorado State Patrol (CSP) to temporarily suspend certain provisions of C.R.S. § 42-4-235, as outlined by CSP, to the extent that they prevent the delivery of necessary fuel to distribution points within Colorado, subject to the following conditions: i. This Executive Order notwithstanding, all drivers, companies, and entities involved in the transportation and delivery of fuel shall prioritize safe practices in all phases of transportation and delivery of fuel. Further, this exception shall not be construed as an exemption from C.R.S. Title 42, Traffic Code, as it relates to general motor vehicle safety, state and federal financial responsibility requirements, commercial driver’s license Executive Order D 2023 004 January 30, 2023 Page 3 of 3 requirements, size and weight regulations, or any federal motor carrier safety regulations not specifically identified herein. ii. This exception shall also not be construed as an exemption from 49 C.F.R. § 392.3 which prohibits ill or fatigued drivers from operating a motor vehicle. iii. Motor carriers or drivers currently subject to an out-of-service order issued by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration are not eligible for the exception until that order expires or the conditions of the order have been met. E. I urge the Attorney General’s Office to pursue any violations of the Colorado Consumer Protection Act, C.R.S. § 6-1-730 et seq., relating to the price of fuel, including charging excessive prices and engaging in price gouging. III. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from January 30, 2023, unless extended further by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this thirtieth day of January, 2023. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: Executive Order D 2023 010 May 16, 2023 Page 3 of 3 D 2023 010 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Gageby Creek Fire in Bent County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2, of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Gageby Creek Fire in Bent County, enabling State agencies to coordinate for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts. I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire.” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). The Gageby Creek Fire started on April 18, 2023, in Bent County. Strong and shifting erratic winds spread the fire in multiple directions, covering 3,040 acres. Due to drought conditions and the high winds, numerous other smaller fires started in multiple fire districts, and combined with the Gageby Creek Fire to exceed the capacity of local agencies. Within one day, the fire grew an additional 1,667 acres. On April 20, 2023, at approximately 8:35 AM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Gageby Creek Fire in Bent County and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. As of April 22, the fire spread to 4,618 acres on State and private lands and was 60% contained. By April 23, 2023, the fire was 90% contained. The Gageby Creek Fire was completely contained on April 28, 2023, at approximately 11:00 AM. II. Declarations and Directives A. The Gageby Creek Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of April 20, 2023, declaring a Executive Order D 2023 010 May 16, 2023 Page 2 of 3 disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. My verbal order of April 20, 2023, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Funds in the Emergency Fire Fund are hereby found insufficient to pay for the State fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Gageby Creek Fire. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Gageby Creek Fire. Therefore, I order that three hundred forty thousand dollars ($340,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber three hundred forty thousand dollars ($340,000) in the DEF, established in C.R.S. § 24-33.5- 706(2)(a), for costs associated with the State’s fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Gageby Creek Fire. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. The funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for this purpose until thirty-six (36) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall be transferred back to the SERCF. E. The Division of Fire Prevention and Control, via its fire billing practices, is authorized to coordinate application for any funds available related to this disaster emergency. Specifically, the Colorado Division of Fire Prevention and Control is directed to seek reimbursement and make payments as needed to agencies providing assistance on this incident. Executive Order D 2023 010 May 16, 2023 Page 3 of 3 II. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from April 20, 2023, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for the described purposes for thirty-six (36) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this sixteenth day of May, 2023. Jared Polis Governor

I. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin including but not limited to severe weather ….” C.R.S § 24 -33.5-703(3). Beginning June 8, 2023, and continuing through June 24, 2023, Colorado experienced a destructive and disruptive summer flood, flash flood, tornado, and severe weather season. The above average precipitation caused an increase in flash flooding to well above normal. Heavy rainfall, combined with saturated soils, caused washouts on county roads in multiple counties. Excess rainfall created numerous washouts of roadways, hiking trails, and retaining walls. The massive amount of rain created sinkholes in multiple counties across the state, resulting in detours on major transportation routes. Drainage ditches became overwhelmed with water carrying debris into ponds, lakes, and rivers. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the June 2023 Severe Weather and Flooding. Over the course of two weeks, Colorado experienced at least 41 tornadoes of varying intensities, including two rated EF-3 on the Enhanced Fujita Tornado Rate Scale, causing extensive damage to trees and structures. Tornadoes were identified along the Front Range and on the Eastern Plains. Tornadoes in Baca and Prowers Counties destroyed homes and damaged electrical infrastructure. High winds in Kiowa County damaged electrical infrastructure. The Executive Order D 2023 019 September 22, 2023 Page 2 of 3 same weather system that created these tornadoes and high winds also caused hail damage to historical structures in Jefferson County. On June 22, 2023, at approximately 4:45 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the June 2023 Severe Weather and Flooding in El Paso, Elbert, Lincoln, and Washington Counties and activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan. On July 18, 2023, at approximately 3:00 PM, after further assessments with the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), I verbally extended the disaster emergency declaration and expanded the declaration to include Arapahoe, Cheyenne, Douglas, Kit Carson, and Logan Counties. After further investigation, it was determined that the damage from severe weather and flooding extended to counties not included in Executive Order D 2023 011. I am therefore declaring a disaster emergency to address severe weather impacts, including high winds, flooding, hail, and tornado damage in Baca, Jefferson, Kiowa, Prowers, and Teller Counties. These counties have sustained significant infrastructure damage from the severe weather events in June 2023. A roadway in Teller County was damaged by flooding. Baca, Prowers, and Kiowa Counties have sustained damage to electrical infrastructure, and Jefferson County buildings have sustained approximately $3 million worth of uncovered hail damage. II. C. I direct State agencies to pursue all available federal funding for response and recovery operations, including but not limited to the Federal Emergency Management Agency, Small Business Administration, and the United States Department of Agriculture. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) were insufficient to pay for response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the June 2023 Severe Weather and Flooding, as set out in Executive Order D 2023 011. full_text: Executive Order D 2023 021 October 27, 2023 Page 1 of 3 D 2023 021 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Iron Fire in Moffat County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Iron Fire in Moffat County, enabling State and federal agencies to coordinate fire suppression, response, consequence management, statewide hazard mitigation, and recovery efforts. Sustained high winds and low relative humidity resulted in extreme fire behavior and rapid rates of spread. The fire threatened multiple ranches and residences, along with electrical and gas utilities, burning 5,443 acres on the first day. Pre-evacuations were put in place and local capacity to address the fire was exceeded. On September 30, 2023, at approximately 9:09 AM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Iron Fire in Moffat County and activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan. On October 3, 2023, responsibility for the Iron Fire was returned to the Moffat County Sheriff’s Office. As of October 9, 2023, the Iron Fire was 100% contained. B. My verbal order of September 30, 2023, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Funds in the Emergency Fire Fund are hereby found insufficient to pay for the State fire suppression, response, consequence management, statewide hazard mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Iron Fire. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, statewide hazard mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Iron Fire. Executive Order D 2023 021 October 27, 2023 Page 3 of 3 III. full_text: Executive Order D 2023 023 October 31, 2023 Page 1 of 2 D 2023 023 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2023 state coordinated election. I. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support on October 31, 2023, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2023 state coordinated election. By activating up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election defense efforts up to and including the 2023 state coordinated election on November 7, 2023. Executive Order D 2023 023 October 31, 2023 Page 2 of 2 II. Declarations and Directives On October 9, 2023, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2023 state coordinated election occurring on November 7, 2023. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, the Governor may employ the National Guard for the defense of the State. I hereby activate up to nine (9) members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to participate in training activities and assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts on October 31, 2023, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2023 state coordinated election. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado, this thirty-first day of October, 2023. Jared Polis Governor

On April 18, 2024, upon further inspection and non-destructive testing of the Blue Mesa Bridge, Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) and CDOT engineers determined that the visual surface crack and internal defects within the butt weld of the Blue Mesa Bridge were critical findings that required closure of the Blue Mesa Bridge in order to protect the safety of the traveling public. The engineers immediately closed the Blue Mesa Bridge to traffic. Executive Order D 2024 006 May 22, 2024 Page 2 of 3 The Blue Mesa Bridge provides a necessary connection to utilize U.S. 50, the main transportation route in the region. The closure of the Blue Mesa Bridge creates significant strains on the local economy, health and medical services including emergency care, education, agricultural activities, and daily travel to and from work for community members. While two alternate state routes have been identified to bypass the Blue Mesa Bridge closure, both routes create five to six-hour commutes for community members and businesses. In addition, the use of these alternate routes is likely to have an adverse impact on the roadway systems in surrounding towns, cities, and counties which are not accustomed to a high volume of traffic. As part of the disaster emergency, the State is investing in maintaining county routes to help them absorb more traffic. On April 23, 2024, at approximately 3:13 PM, the Lieutenant Governor, acting as Governor, verbally declared a state of disaster emergency due to the Blue Mesa Bridge closure in Gunnison, Hinsdale, and Montrose Counties, and activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan. The Lieutenant Governor also verbally authorized employment and use of the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of responding to the Blue Mesa Bridge closure and providing support, assisting law enforcement agencies with traffic control, and supporting incident management. Declarations and Directives A. The U.S. 50 Blue Mesa Middle Bridge closure and associated impacts in Gunnison, Hinsdale, and Montrose Counties constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. The Lieutenant Governor’s verbal order of April 23, 2024, declaring a disaster emergency, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained in this Executive Order. B. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, the Lieutenant Governor’s verbal order of April 23, 2024, authorizing employment and use of the Colorado National Guard in an unarmed capacity for the purpose of responding to the Blue Mesa Bridge closure and providing support, assisting law enforcement agencies with traffic control, and supporting incident management, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained in this Executive Order. C. The Lieutenant Governor’s verbal order of April 23, 2024, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies were authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. Executive Order D 2024 006 May 22, 2024 Page 3 of 3 D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Blue Mesa Bridge closure. Therefore, I order that five million dollars ($5,000,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber five million dollars ($5,000,000) in the DEF to pay for response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Blue Mesa Bridge closure. E. I direct State agencies to pursue all available federal funding for response and recovery operations, including but not limited to the Federal Highway Administration, U.S. Department of Transportation, and U.S. Department of Agriculture. F. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding described in Section II.D to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of funds. The funds described in Section II.D shall remain available for this purpose for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the DEF. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from April 23, 2024, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.D of this Executive Order shall remain available for the described purposes for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this twenty-second day of May, 2024. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: Executive Order D 2024 007 June 10, 2024 Page 1 of 2 D 2024 007 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2024 Primary Election. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but it could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support on June 18, 2024, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2024 Primary Election. By activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election cyber defense efforts up to and including the 2024 Primary Election on June 25, 2024. full_text: Executive Order D 2024 008 August 2, 2024 Page 1 of 4 D 2024 008 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring and Extending a Disaster Emergency Due to Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Weld County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring and extending a state of disaster emergency due to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Weld County, enabling State agencies to better support our agriculture sector by coordinating for statewide monitoring and mitigation of disease spread, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts, and enabling statewide surveillance and additional statewide protective measures for Grade A dairy operations. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S § 24-33.5-703(3). Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI) was initially detected in the United States in the wild bird population in January 2022 in South Carolina and in the domestic poultry population in February 2022 in Indiana. HPAI has spread across the United States over the past 2.5 years. The disease spreads rapidly among wild and domestic poultry. It has a mortality rate above ninety percent in poultry. HPAI was detected in wild birds in Colorado on March 24, 2022, with ongoing detection in the State since that time. Cases in Colorado are occurring in wild, domestic, and commercial flocks, including occasional spillover into mammals. In March 2024, the USDA confirmed the detection of HPAI (H5N1 avian flu virus) in dairy cattle in the Texas Panhandle region. Since then, the virus has spread to 12 states, impacting more than 163 dairies. The spread of this virus has been via cow-to-cow and farm-to- farm transmission. Unlike in previous outbreaks, the virus is not currently being spread by wild birds. Colorado has the highest number of reported cases of HPAI in dairy herds in the United States, with 50 confirmed detections. Executive Order D 2024 008 August 2, 2024 Page 2 of 4 On July 5, 2024, HPAI was confirmed in a commercial table egg layer facility in Weld County, affecting 1.8 million birds. On July 15, 2024, HPAI was confirmed in a second commercial egg layer facility in Weld County, affecting approximately 1.4 million birds. A third commercial facility in Weld County was confirmed on July 19, 2024, impacting approximately 300,000 birds. The same day, five human HPAI infections in workers at the site were also confirmed by the Colorado Department of Public Health & Environment. As of July 23, 2024, a total of 10 people have confirmed infections associated with the current outbreak in Weld County. Through genomic sequencing, it was determined that the strain of the virus in the poultry facilities is the same as that found in the affected dairies. This suggests that infected dairy cattle may be a significant source of the virus infecting poultry. Oversight of the response to the outbreak in livestock and implementation of statewide surveillance and protective measures requires the deployment and coordination of multiple State agencies, including the Colorado Department of Agriculture, Colorado Department of Public Health & Environment, Colorado Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management, and federal partners including the United States Department of Agriculture and Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. On July 5, 2024, at approximately 7:00 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency for the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Weld County and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. This Executive Order memorializes that verbal declaration and extends the declaration of a disaster emergency for an additional thirty (30) days due to the ongoing need to identify HPAI cases and due to the potential for further response to affected facilities. Declarations and Directives A. HPAI in Weld County and associated statewide impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of July 5, 2024, declaring a disaster emergency is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is hereby activated. All State departments and agencies shall take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or Acting Director of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the Emergency Support Function 5 Annex of the State Emergency Operations Executive Order D 2024 008 August 2, 2024 Page 3 of 4 Plan, and the Food and Agriculture Incident Annex of the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Personal Protective Equipment at the Office of Emergency Management’s Resource Asset Management site shall be made available to protect the health and safety of response workers and support personnel at the affected sites, and to minimize further spread of HPAI. D. I authorize expanded statewide testing and surveillance of Grade A dairy facilities to minimize and contain the spread of HPAI. I authorize oversight of response activities, including depopulation, for impacted commercial poultry locations in Weld County. I also authorize HPAI testing and treatment for human workers at response sites. E. Funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are hereby found insufficient to pay for statewide monitoring and mitigation of disease spread, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to HPAI. Therefore, I order that three million five hundred thousand dollars ($3,500,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber three million five hundred thousand dollars ($3,500,000) in the DEF, established in C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(2)(a), for costs associated with the State’s statewide monitoring and mitigation of disease spread, response, consequence management, and recovery efforts related to the Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Colorado since July 5, 2024. F. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and non-profit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of the funds. The funds described in Section II.E above shall remain available for this purpose until seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the Disaster Emergency Fund. G. The Office of Emergency Management, in coordination with the Colorado Department of Agriculture and the Colorado Department of Public Health & Environment, is authorized to coordinate application for any funds available related to this disaster emergency. Specifically, the Colorado Department of Agriculture is directed to seek reimbursement, including reimbursement from the United States Department of Agriculture for response activities under the 2024 Executive Order D 2024 008 August 2, 2024 Page 4 of 4 Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza Emergency Cooperative Agreement, and make payments as needed to agencies providing assistance on this incident. Duration This Executive Order, declaring and extending the disaster emergency, shall expire thirty (30) days from August 3, 2024, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II.E above shall remain available for the described purposes for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this second day of August, 2024. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: Executive Order D 2024 015 October 10, 2024 Page 1 of 2 D 2024 015 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2024 General Election. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but it could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support on October 10, 2024, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2024 General Election. By activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election cyber defense efforts up to and including the 2024 General Election on November 5, 2024. Executive Order D 2024 015 October 10, 2024 Page 2 of 2 Declarations and Directives On September 6, 2024, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2024 General Election occurring on November 5, 2024. I hereby activate no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to participate in training activities and assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts on October 10, 2024, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2024 General Election. Around 10:30 a.m. on December 30, 2021, a grass fire, paired with straight-line winds in excess of one hundred miles per hour, quickly spread to populated areas within Boulder County and threatened lives and structures.
