full_text: Executive Order D 2025 002 February 7, 2025 Page 1 of 3 D 2025 002 EXECUTIVE ORDER Amending Provisions of Executive Order D 2024 014 Concerning the Disaster Emergency Due to Flooding and Debris Flow in Ouray County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2 of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, issue this Executive Order to amend provisions of Executive Order D 2024 014 due to additional damage to State infrastructure identified in Montrose County by the Colorado Department of Transportation (CDOT) as a result of the same monsoonal weather system, and providing CDOT the ability to seek federal reimbursement for eligible expenses. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). Beginning August 5, 2024, rain from a monsoonal weather system caused flash flooding, landslides, and debris flows in Ouray County. Numerous roads became damaged and impassable and debris flows rerouted Beaver Creek, destroying the Town of Ridgeway’s drinking water collection system. On August 23, 2024, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Flooding and Debris Flow in Ouray County and activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. On September 20, 2024, I issued Executive Order D 2024 014 memorializing my verbal declaration of a disaster emergency. On August 12, 2024, monsoonal storms produced a flood surge causing severe damage to the abutment embankment of bridge K-01-B, carrying CO 141 (MM 85.52) over the Dolores River, located in Montrose County. The precipitation runoff from the storm took place in a wildfire affected burn scar watershed which drains into a tributary stream feeding into the Dolores River, creating a 25 year flood surge in the location of the bridge. Massive damage took place to the south abutment embankment (Abutment 1) leaving approximately 25 feet of exposed abutment piling, compromising the approach roadway at the end of the bridge. Upon further Executive Order D 2025 002 February 7, 2025 Page 2 of 3 inspection, additional damage was discovered to the adjacent pier (Pier 1), a primary foundational element required to safely hold up the adjacent spans of the bridge. The localized scour had also compromised the soil supporting the footing under Pier 1, leaving the bridge susceptible to failure during a future flooding event. Temporary repairs have been implemented by placing a layer of large stones to protect the soil from erosion (rip rap) around the existing damaged areas. However, CDOT needs to complete permanent repairs before the 2025 spring runoff to avoid further closures and disruptions to the lives of Coloradans. The permanent repairs require reinforcement with the use of micro piles around the foundation at Pier 1 to meet the requirements to resist future flooding events. The repairs will additionally include armoring of the embankment and channel around Abutment 1. CO 141 is a critical route connecting the rural communities of Norwood, Nucla, and Naturita to the City of Grand Junction for critical agricultural supplies and medical needs. If this bridge is closed, the detour route is 230 miles, or approximately 4 hours. County roads are not available as detours due to the rough canyon terrain that the highway travels. In December 2024, CDOT determined that repair expenses are expected to exceed three million dollars ($3,000,000) and may be eligible for federal reimbursement through the Federal Highway Administration (FHWA). This amendment to the Executive Order provides CDOT the ability to seek federal reimbursement for eligible expenses related to the bridge repair. Amendments 1. Executive Order D 2024 014 is amended to include Montrose County in the disaster declaration due to extensive and serious damage to bridge K-01-B on CO 141 in Montrose County. 2. Section II.E of Executive Order D 2024 014 is amended to add as follows: E. I authorize CDOT to pursue federal transportation emergency relief funds under sections 120 and 125 of Title 23 of the United States Code. I request that the FHWA Division Administrator concur in the declaration of this disaster emergency for the purposes of securing FHWA Emergency Relief Program Funds to provide CDOT with personnel and resources to assist with slide area monitoring, mudslides and debris flows cleanup operations, and repair of any damaged or destroyed highway assets for CDOT Bridge Structure K-01-B, located at mile marker 85.52 on CO 141 in Montrose County. full_text: Executive Order D 2025 010 August 8, 2025 Page 1 of 3 D 2025 010 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to a Severe Weather Event Resulting in Dangerous Fire Conditions in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2, of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to a severe weather event resulting in dangerous fire conditions in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties, enabling State agencies to coordinate fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire.” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). On July 10, 2025, a widespread and severe weather event resulted in dangerous fire conditions leading to more than twenty lightning-caused wildfires burning uncontained across the western slope of Colorado (Western Colorado Fires). These fires include the South Rim Fire in Montrose County, the Turner Gulch Fire in Mesa County, and the Deer Creek Fire in Montrose County, among others. The South Rim Fire burned in the Black Canyon of the Gunnison, forcing the closure of the North Rim portion of the Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park until July 30, 2025, and the South Rim portion of the National Park was still closed due to firefighting, repair, and rehabilitation efforts as of August 6, 2025. The Turner Gulch Fire resulted in the closure of Colorado Highway 141 and evacuations of dozens of residences. The Deer Creek Fire started in eastern Utah, transferred into Colorado, burned into Montrose County, and threatened the Highway 90 corridor and the community of Paradox. The Western Colorado Fires were located in remote areas in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties on Bureau of Land Management, National Park Service, United States Forest Service, and State and private lands, with steep, inaccessible terrain, and heavy fuels that did not allow for access and safe engagement on the fires. The fires continued to grow, threatening homes and infrastructure, and exceeding normal fire resource and incident management capabilities of the affected counties. A preliminary assessment shows that the Western Colorado Fires have damaged a number of structures, including a United States Forest Service cabin, two Executive Order D 2025 010 August 8, 2025 Page 2 of 3 outbuildings, and a pavilion. Additionally, within a three mile radius of the fires, an electrical substation and powerplant were threatened. On July 13, 2025, at approximately 11:42 AM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to a severe weather event resulting in dangerous fire conditions in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties and activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan and directed the Office of Emergency Management (OEM) to take all necessary and appropriate State actions to assist the affected jurisdictions with their fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts. As of August 6, 2025, the South Rim Fire was 52% contained, the Turner Gulch Fire was 49% contained, and the Deer Creek Fire was 95% contained. Declarations and Directives A. The severe weather event resulting in dangerous fire conditions and the subsequent Western Colorado Fires and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of July 13, 2025, declaring a disaster emergency, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. My verbal order of July 13, 2025 activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies are authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the OEM pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment, as necessary. C. I direct State agencies to pursue all available federal funding for response and recovery operations. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the severe weather event resulting in dangerous fire conditions and the subsequent Western Colorado Fires. Therefore, I order that one million eight hundred eighty-nine thousand seven hundred dollars ($1,889,700) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber one million eight hundred eighty- nine thousand seven hundred dollars ($1,889,700) in the DEF to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the severe weather event resulting in dangerous fire conditions and the subsequent Western Colorado Fires. E. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the OEM is authorized and directed to allocate the funding described in Section II(D) to the appropriate Executive Order D 2025 010 August 8, 2025 Page 3 of 3 government agencies and nonprofit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of funds. The funds described in Section II(D) above shall remain available for this purpose until seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the DEF. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from July 13, 2025, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(D) above shall remain available for the described purposes for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this eighth day of August, 2025. Jared Polis Governor

The state benefits from early engagement of fires with resources and operational support immediately following detection of new fire starts when possible and appropriate. Early attack on fires can keep those fires from becoming costlier and more dangerous events. This Executive Order supports the Division of Fire Prevention and Control (DFPC) within the Department of Public Safety (DPS) to continue its practice of initial aggressive attack in the early stages of developing fires, working with local agencies to provide prepositioning of resources prior to fires occurring or when they are first detected, with overhead support, aviation, handcrews, modules, engines, and other assets eligible for Wildfire Emergency Response Funding (WERF) pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-1226 and Attachment A of the 2025 Wildland Fire Preparedness Plan. This strategy supports community safety and prevents economic loss. Executive Order D 2025 012 August 14, 2025 Page 2 of 5 Colorado is facing a challenging fire season. On July 10, 2025, a widespread and severe weather event resulted in dangerous fire conditions leading to more than twenty lightning-caused wildfires burning across the western slope in multiple counties, including the South Rim and Deer Creek Fires in Montrose County, the Turner Gulch Fire in Mesa County, and the Sowbelly Fire, which burned in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties. On July 13, 2025, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to these conditions in Delta, Mesa, and Montrose Counties, and memorialized this declaration in Executive Order D 2025 010. On August 3, 2025, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Elk Fire in Rio Blanco County, which burned on private and state-owned land. Additionally, at least two other fires were burning in Rio Blanco County, the Lee and Grease Fires, which initially were completely on federal Bureau of Land Management (BLM) land and later spread to federal, state, and private land. On August 5, the Lee and Grease Fires combined into one large fire, designated the Lee Fire, which has since burned and grown rapidly, displacing residents due to evacuations and placing others on pre-evacuation status. The Elk and Lee Fires burned within 15 miles of each other near the town of Meeker. On August 5, 2025, I expanded the initial disaster declaration for the Elk Fire to include the Lee Fire. On August 6, I authorized employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to respond to the Elk and Lee Fires by providing fire suppression support. The FMAG authorized the use of federal funds to help with firefighting costs. On August 4, 2025, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the LeRoux Fire in Delta County, which burned on private and BLM land. As of August 5, the fire had a fire path towards heavy fuels and a potential for aggressive and expansive growth. The LeRoux Fire necessitated evacuations of primary homes and 152 homes were on pre-evacuation status, and an additional 60 structures were threatened. As of August 13, the LeRoux Fire had burned 195 acres. On August 10, 2025, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Oak Fire in Archuleta County near Pagosa Springs, which burned multiple structures and caused numerous evacuations on private land in the Wildland Urban Interface. The Oak Fire has threatened over 5,100 buildings and 2,000 homes. I also authorized employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to respond to the Oak Fire as requested by the Department of Public Executive Order D 2025 012 August 14, 2025 Page 3 of 5 Safety. On August 11, FEMA approved a FMAG for the Oak Fire, determining that the fire threatened such destruction that it would constitute a major disaster. On August 13, 2025, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Crosho Fire outside Yampa in Rio Blanco and Routt Counties. The Crosho Fire started burning on August 11 on federal land, and later spread to private land. Routt County issued evacuation notices beginning on August 12, and additional evacuations were ordered on August 13. As of the evening of August 13, the Crosho Fire covered 1,700 acres, including 600 acres of private land. I also authorized employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to respond to the Crosho Fire as requested by the Department of Public Safety. The fire danger has remained at near record levels across much of Colorado, and elevated fire weather and fire risk is forecast for the coming weeks. State, federal, and local communities are mobilizing equipment and personnel to conduct fire suppression and support activities. Colorado’s state and local response has been remarkable to date; there are currently 2,395 personnel supporting nine large fires burning on more than 185,000 acres in Colorado. The firefighting efforts include 41 aircraft, including federal, state, Colorado National Guard, and county assets, working on multiple fronts. Our own State agencies are contributing as well. The Division of Fire Prevention and Control, Division of Homeland Security and Emergency Management and the Colorado State Patrol have all contributed more than 100 personnel and resources in the form of firefighters and engines, recovery and damage assessment teams, traffic control, and other resources. These efforts are bolstered by early attack, and this strategy has helped to prevent large fires from becoming worse and more dangerous events, giving a leg up to the state’s collective firefighting efforts. It is essential that the State continue to take steps to mitigate risk and prepare for additional fires while also working to manage fires quickly after they begin. The state has developed new firefighting capabilities that allow our response to be more nimble than in the past. Accordingly, I am declaring a state of disaster emergency due to multiple fires in Colorado and continued fire risk in Colorado. Given the fire activity in Colorado and ongoing requests for state assistance from local agencies this fiscal year, the WERF, created by statute and meant to provide funding and reimbursement for various wildfire response expenses, is nearly depleted. DFPC has provided funding for local agencies out of the WERF on multiple incidents in support of rapid and aggressive initial fire suppression response. WERF funding is meant to prevent new, emerging fires from growing to become the responsibility of the State, and threatening life, property, infrastructure, watersheds, and communications, while easing pressure on limited resources and reducing overall suppression, recovery, insurance, and other costs. Depletion of the WERF is imminent. I encumber two million five hundred thousand dollars ($2,500,000) in the DEF to fund the transfer described in Section II(F) below. F. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4.5)(b), because I deem it necessary based on my determination that a wildfire-related disaster emergency is imminent, I hereby direct the State Treasurer to transfer funds from the DEF to the WERF. full_text: Executive Order D 2025 013 August 22, 2025 Page 1 of 3 D 2025 013 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Hazardous Materials Incident in Pueblo County Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2, of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Hazardous Materials Incident in Pueblo County, enabling State agencies to coordinate response, consequence management, and hazard mitigation efforts. The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damages, injury or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin.” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). On or around August 20, 2025, inspectors of the Office of Funeral and Mortuary Science Services in the Colorado Department of Regulatory Agencies (DORA) arrived at Davis Mortuary, a funeral home in Pueblo, for a statutorily mandated annual inspection. Inspectors found several bodies in various stages of decomposition in a concealed room. Based on this inspection, on August 20, 2025, the Director of the Division of Professions and Occupations, who oversees the Office of Funeral and Mortuary Science Services, summarily suspended Davis Mortuary’s registration to practice as a funeral establishment pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-4-104(4)(a) pending proceedings to determine whether Davis Mortuary’s registration to practice should be further disciplined. The Director further ordered, pending the outcome of the proceedings, Davis Mortuary to “immediately cease, desist, and refrain from any further acts for which a registration to practice as a funeral establishment is required by the laws of the state of Colorado.” On August 21, 2025, the City of Pueblo, Pueblo County Sheriff’s Office, and the Board of County Commissioners of Pueblo County declared a local disaster in Pueblo County due to the situation at Davis Mortuary and the involvement of the elected Pueblo County Coroner. As stated in the local disaster declaration, Pueblo County is currently without an acting Coroner, Coroner’s Office, or adequate staffing; there are anticipated hazardous materials involved; there Executive Order D 2025 013 August 22, 2025 Page 2 of 3 are expected costs that are anticipated to exceed that of Pueblo City and the Pueblo County governments; and there is an expected need for State-owned resources. Pueblo County officials and the City of Pueblo Police Department requested assistance from the State. Accordingly, because improperly cared for remains represent a public health hazard, I am declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Hazardous Materials Incident in Pueblo County, enabling State agencies to coordinate response, consequence management, and hazard mitigation efforts. Declarations and Directives A. The Hazardous Materials Incident and associated impacts in Pueblo County constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. This Executive Order declares a disaster emergency beginning today, August 22, 2025. B. The State Emergency Operations Plan is activated. All State departments and agencies are authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the Office of Emergency Management, pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment as necessary. C. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for response, consequence management, and hazard mitigation efforts related to the Hazardous Materials Incident in Pueblo County. Therefore, I order that three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber three hundred thousand dollars ($300,000) in the DEF to pay for response, consequence management, and hazard mitigation efforts related to the Hazardous Materials Incident in Pueblo County. D. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the Office of Emergency Management is hereby authorized and directed to allocate the funding to the appropriate government agencies and nonprofit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of funds. The funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for this purpose until seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the DEF. E. I encourage Pueblo County officials and the Pueblo County Deputy Coroner to seek assistance from other counties, including deputizing neighboring County Coroners and their staff, and for those counties to provide assistance to Pueblo Executive Order D 2025 013 August 22, 2025 Page 3 of 3 County in the investigation, management, and mitigation of this disaster, as well as in the day-to-day operations of the Pueblo County Coroner's Office. F. I call upon the Pueblo County Coroner to resign from office immediately to ensure continuity of essential services in Pueblo County. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from August 22, 2025, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(C) above shall remain available for the described purposes for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order. full_text: Executive Order D 2025 018 September 8, 2025 Page 1 of 3 D 2025 018 EXECUTIVE ORDER Declaring a Disaster Emergency Due to the Crosho Fire in Rio Blanco and Routt Counties and Authorizing Employment of the Colorado National Guard Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 2, of the Colorado Constitution and the relevant portions of the Colorado Disaster Emergency Act, C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, issue this Executive Order declaring a state of disaster emergency due to the Crosho Fire in Rio Blanco and Routt Counties, enabling State and federal agencies to coordinate fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts. Further, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3- 104, I authorized employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard for the purpose of supporting fire suppression efforts as deemed necessary by the Colorado Department of Public Safety for the Crosho Fire. Background and Purpose The Governor is responsible for meeting the dangers to the State and people presented by disasters. C.R.S. § 24-33.5-704(1). The Colorado Disaster Emergency Act defines a disaster as “the occurrence or imminent threat of widespread or severe damage, injury, or loss of life or property resulting from any natural cause or cause of human origin, including but not limited to fire.” C.R.S. § 24-33.5-703(3). On August 11, 2025, the Crosho Fire started burning near the border of Rio Blanco and Routt Counties on federal land and later spread to private land. Routt County issued evacuation notices beginning on August 12, and additional evacuations were ordered on August 13. By the evening of August 13, the Crosho Fire covered 1,700 acres, including 600 acres of private land. The fire exceeded the capacity of the counties based on the hazardous fuels conditions, exhibited fire behavior, incident complexity, and the external aviation and ground resources needed to manage the incident. Additionally, Rio Blanco County was already experiencing two other large fires (Elk and Lee Fires) at the same time. As referenced in Executive Order D 2025 012, on August 13, 2025, at approximately 8:40 PM, I verbally declared a disaster emergency due to the Crosho Fire in Rio Blanco and Routt Counties, and activated the State of Colorado Emergency Operations Plan and directed the Executive Order D 2025 018 September 8, 2025 Page 2 of 3 Office of Emergency Management (OEM) to take all necessary and appropriate State actions to assist the affected jurisdictions with their fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts. At the same time, I verbally authorized employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to respond to the Crosho Fire by providing fire suppression support. As of August 25, 2025, the Crosho Fire burned 2,073 acres and was 100% contained. Declarations and Directives A. The Crosho Fire and associated impacts constitute a disaster emergency under C.R.S. § 24-33.5-701, et seq. My verbal order of August 13, 2025, declaring a disaster emergency, is hereby memorialized by this Executive Order and shall have the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. B. My verbal order of August 13, 2025, activated the State Emergency Operations Plan. All State departments and agencies are authorized to take whatever actions may be required and requested by the Director or their delegate of the OEM pursuant to the State Emergency Operations Plan, including provision of appropriate staff and equipment, as necessary. C. Further, pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, this Executive Order hereby memorializes my verbal orders of August 13, 2025, authorizing employing unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard to support fire suppression efforts as deemed necessary by the Colorado Department of Public Safety for the Crosho Fire, and my verbal authorization has the full force and effect of law as if it were contained within this Executive Order. D. I direct State agencies to pursue all available federal funding for response and recovery operations. E. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-706(4)(b), funds in the Disaster Emergency Fund (DEF) are insufficient to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Crosho Fire. Therefore, I order that three million eight hundred fifty seven thousand dollars ($3,857,000) be transferred from the State Emergency Reserve Cash Fund (SERCF) to the DEF. I encumber three million eight hundred fifty seven thousand dollars ($3,857,000) in the DEF to pay for fire suppression, response, consequence management, mitigation, and recovery efforts related to the Crosho Fire. Executive Order D 2025 018 September 8, 2025 Page 3 of 3 F. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 24-33.5-705.4(5), the Director of the OEM is authorized and directed to allocate the funding described in Section II(E) to the appropriate government agencies and nonprofit organizations and execute awards, purchase orders, or other mechanisms to effect the allocation of funds. The funds described in Section II(E) shall remain available for this purpose until seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order, and any unexpended funds shall remain in the DEF. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from August 13, 2025, unless extended further by Executive Order, except that the funds described in Section II(E) above shall remain available for the described purposes for seventy-two (72) months from the date of this Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this eighth day of September, 2025. Jared Polis Governor

full_text: Executive Order D 2025 019 October 21, 2025 Page 1 of 2 D 2025 019 EXECUTIVE ORDER Activating the Colorado National Guard to Assist with Election Cybersecurity Defense Efforts Pursuant to the authority vested in the Governor of the State of Colorado and, in particular, pursuant to Article IV, Section 5 of the Colorado Constitution and C.R.S. § 28-3-104, et seq., I, Jared Polis, Governor of the State of Colorado, hereby issue this Executive Order activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts during the 2025 Coordinated Election. Background and Purpose Like many states, Colorado uses online voter registration systems that allow eligible citizens to access and update their voter registration information. These systems are protected by various security features that maintain confidentiality and prevent data tampering or interference with data. Even with such security features, online voter registration systems could provide an avenue for cyber actors to gain unlawful access to voter registration databases. Outside of Colorado, voter registration databases have been compromised by cyber actors hacking into various systems. While cyber actors are unable to modify voter records, breaches could result in the release of voters’ personally identifiable information. The exposure of voters’ personally identifiable information does not threaten the integrity of our State elections, but it could undermine public confidence in the system and suppress voter registration. The Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element has unique cyber capabilities to assist in protecting critical election infrastructure. The Colorado Secretary of State has requested that the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element provide election cybersecurity support on October 21, 2025, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2025 Coordinated Election. By activating no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element, the National Guard will support the Secretary of State with election cyber defense efforts up to and including the 2025 Coordinated Election on November 4, 2025. Executive Order D 2025 019 October 21, 2025 Page 2 of 2 Declarations and Directives On October 16, 2025, the Colorado Secretary of State requested support from the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element for the 2025 Coordinated Election occurring on November 4, 2025. Pursuant to C.R.S. § 28-3-104, the Governor may employ the National Guard for the defense of the State. I hereby activate no less than four (4) and up to six (6) unarmed members of the Colorado National Guard Defensive Cyber Operations Element to participate in training activities and assist with election cybersecurity defense efforts on October 21, 2025, and extending for up to thirty (30) days, for the 2025 Coordinated Election. Duration This Executive Order shall expire thirty (30) days from October 21, 2025, unless extended further by Executive Order. GIVEN under my hand and the Executive Seal of the State of Colorado this twenty-first day of October, 2025. Jared Polis Governor
